description: Left navigation shell. Input: the current route. Output: a nav rail rendering exactly three entries labelled Operational Picture, Hypotheses, Scenario Control, with the entry matching the current route marked active and exposed as the current page to assistive tech. Constraints: exactly three entries, no fourth; drill-down tables and system health are not entries. Failure case: rendering a fourth nav entry, or rendering zero active entries when the route matches a known screen, fails the spec. Refs: FR-701, FR-709, US-A1, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.7. Amended 2026-09-13, before tests, after scn-004 landed a screen nothing could reach. Six decisions. First, the current route is the URL hash: not a router library, and not component state. A library is a dependency taken on for three destinations with no nesting and no parameters; component state makes the URL a lie, so a reload returns the analyst to a screen they did not choose and no screen can be linked to or named in a bug report. The hash costs nothing, survives a reload, and makes each entry a real link -- which is what puts aria-current=page on an anchor where assistive technology expects it, rather than on a button pretending to be one. An empty or unrecognised hash resolves to the Operational Picture rather than rendering nothing. Second, all three destinations render something and two of them exist. Operational Picture is unchanged. Scenario Control renders scn-004's screen. Hypotheses has no screen yet, so its destination says exactly that: FR-701 fixes the rail at three entries, and an entry that renders a blank page is worse than one that names what is missing. Third, the Scenario Control destination states that its runs are a fixture rather than the database. api-006 does not exist, so that table lists the mock -- real seeds from a real batch, but not what the database holds -- and api-003 already settled the principle this turns on: example data presented as though it were the system's own is the failure this project exists to argue against. The screen already carries a note when nothing is wired to its controls, and that note names the table too. Fourth, the poll runs only while the Operational Picture is mounted. App calls api-003's hook unconditionally today; with three destinations that keeps a five-second poll running against an endpoint nobody is looking at. The hook moves into the destination that uses it, which leaves api-003's seam where it was -- one place that knows the picture is fetched rather than passed in. Fifth, the three screens are declared once, in one list, and the rail is a dumb component over it. Exactly-three is then assertable at the source as well as in the DOM; two lists would be two places to add a fourth. Sixth, the rail carries no system-health strip and no drill-down entries. Health is a strip in the shell rather than an entry (FR-709), and it is not this item's. Failure cases added: an unrecognised hash rendering no screen at all; and the Scenario Control destination presenting fixture rows with nothing on screen saying they are fixture rows. Scope: a route list, the rail, the App wiring, and one sentence added to scn-004's note. It builds no Hypotheses screen and wires no scenario endpoint. Refs adds: scn-004, api-003, api-006, FR-714. Superseded in part 2026-09-13 by api-010, recorded here rather than left as a silent divergence. The third decision above put a sentence on screen saying the listed runs were a fixture, which was true for exactly as long as api-006 did not exist. The runs now come from GET /api/v1/scenario/runs, so that sentence would be false and the note carrying it is gone, together with the test that asserted it. The principle the decision expressed is unchanged and is now enforced from the other side: api-010 asserts the word fixture is absent from the screen once the rows are real, and that no fixture row is ever rendered while the list has not been read. The fourth decision -- the poll belonging to the screen that needs it -- is unchanged and now holds for two screens rather than one; its test counts picture requests by path, because a bare call count rises for the scenario poll as well.

System-health status strip in the nav footer. Input: a system-health value from the operational-picture contract. Output: a compact strip in the navigation footer showing the health state as a categorical label. Constraints: it is a strip, not a screen and not a nav entry; state renders as a categorical label only. Failure case: rendering health as a percentage such as 98% uptime, or promoting health to a fourth nav entry, fails the spec. Refs: FR-702, FR-715, ui-001, nav-001.

Operational Picture status bar. Input: operationalPicture.scenario. Output: a top bar showing the scenario name badge and a persistent data-mode badge reading SYNTHETIC ENVIRONMENT DATA. Constraints: the data-mode badge is unconditional and cannot be dismissed or collapsed; it renders even when scenario data is absent. Failure case: the data-mode badge missing, or hidden behind a loading or empty state, fails the spec. Refs: FR-703, NFR-303, US-A7.

Active hypothesis cards in the right rail. Input: operationalPicture.hypotheses. Output: one card per active hypothesis showing title and confidence as a Low/Medium/High pip; activating a card navigates to that hypothesis on Hypothesis Detail. Constraints: confidence renders via the ui-001 primitive; an empty list renders an explicit no active hypotheses state rather than a blank rail. Failure case: an empty hypothesis list rendering an empty rail with no message, or a card rendering confidence as a number, fails the spec. Refs: FR-707, FR-715, ui-001, hyp-001, US-A4.

Detection summary panel. Input: operationalPicture.detectionSummary. Output: anomaly counts per category plus an overall severity rendered as Low/Medium/High. Constraints: counts are integers and may be shown as integers; severity is categorical only; no anomaly score, signal integrity, or confidence figure is rendered as a percentage or decimal. Failure case: rendering a severity of 0.82 or 82% fails the spec. Refs: FR-707, FR-715, ui-001, NFR-203.

Tabbed exception panel. Input: the operational-picture payload for the current view filter (op-007, api-007). Output: one panel with three tabs labelled RF (n anomalous), Tracks (n degraded), Events, listing the rows the current filter admits, with a footer reading +n nominal hidden and a View all link. Constraints: the default filter state is Anomalous only, so nominal rows are absent from the first render; the hidden count comes from the suppressed-count metadata on the response, not from counting the payload, because server-side filtering means the excluded rows never arrive; n in the tab label equals the number of rows shown. Failure case: a nominal RF sensor appearing while the filter is Anomalous only, or the footer count being derived from the payload and therefore reading zero whenever the backend filtered, fails the spec. Refs: FR-708, FR-716, FR-809, US-A1, op-007, api-007, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.7.

Drill-down tables. Input: activation of the View all link in an exception panel footer (op-004). Output: a full table over the same contract data, showing nominal and anomalous rows: full RF observation stream from the RF tab, full track inventory from the Tracks tab. Constraints: reachable only from panel footers, never from the nav; it is a view over the same data, not a new data source. Failure case: adding a nav entry for a drill-down table, or a drill-down fetching from an endpoint the panel does not use, fails the spec. Refs: FR-709, FR-701, nav-001, op-004.

Timeline strip. Input: operationalPicture.timelineEvents. Output: a horizontal strip rendering each event with its label and time, ordered oldest to newest. Constraints: ordering is by event time and independent of array order in the input; an empty list renders an explicit empty state. Failure case: events supplied out of order rendering out of order, or an empty list rendering a bare strip with no message, fails the spec. Refs: FR-710, hyp-001.

View filter control. Input: analyst selection of Anomalous only, Nominal only, or All. Output: the selection is sent to the backend as the view parameter (api-007), and the returned payload drives the map (map-003) and the exception panel (op-004) together, so the two always agree about what is shown. Constraints: default state is Anomalous only, preserving US-A1; the selection persists across polls rather than resetting on each refresh; drill-down tables stay unfiltered, since they are the show-everything view by definition. Failure case: the map showing all entities while the panel still shows only anomalous ones, or the filter resetting to the default on the next poll tick, fails the spec. Refs: FR-716, FR-809, US-A1, US-A9, op-004, map-003, api-007.

Playback transport control. Input: a scenario run's simulated-time window and analyst interaction with play, pause, speed, and scrub. Output: a playback cursor in simulated time driving the map render (map-004), with the current cursor position displayed. Constraints: the transport operates over simulated scenario time, never wall clock, consistent with anom-009; scrubbing to any point in the window is permitted, including backwards; pausing holds the cursor rather than resetting it. Failure case: playback speed altering the reported simulated time of a rendered position, so that the same cursor shows different data at 1x and 4x, fails the spec. Refs: FR-717, US-A10, anom-009, map-004, api-008, scn-004.

Confidence and severity rendering primitive, the global no-fake-precision invariant. Input: a confidence or severity value. Output: a rendered Low, Medium, or High label or pip. Constraints: the accepted input domain is exactly Low|Medium|High; the component never formats a number into a percentage or decimal; every screen renders confidence and severity through this primitive rather than inline. Failure case: passing 0.87 or 87 renders nothing and surfaces a development-time error rather than displaying 87%. Refs: FR-715, NFR-203, AC-11, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.5.

MapView adapter boundary. Input: aircraft tracks, RF sensors, and anomaly zones from the operational-picture contract. Output: a rendered map with a marker layer per entity kind. Constraints: MapView is the only module in the repo importing MapLibre GL JS or any map library, so it can be mocked wholesale in tests; no other component imports map types or calls map APIs. Failure case: a second module importing maplibre-gl fails the spec, and a repo-wide import check must assert this. Refs: FR-704, FR-705, US-E2, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 10.

MapView graceful placeholder. Input: absent or empty tile-source configuration. Output: a labelled placeholder region showing entity counts and a message that no tile source is configured. Constraints: no crash, no blank region, no thrown error, no network request attempted; the surrounding screen renders normally. Failure case: an unset tile-source env var producing a blank pane or an unhandled exception fails the spec. Refs: FR-705, NFR-102, map-001.

Anomalous items highlighted on the map. Input: tracks, sensors, and anomaly zones each carrying an anomalous or nominal state. Output: anomalous entities render visually distinct from nominal ones and carry a non-visual anomalous marker for tests and assistive tech; selecting one emits a selection event identifying the entity and any linked hypothesis. Constraints: distinctness is asserted through the entity state exposed in the accessible name, not through CSS classes; nominal entities are never highlighted. Failure case: an entity flagged anomalous in the contract rendering identically to a nominal one fails the spec. Refs: FR-706, US-A2, US-A3, map-001, hyp-001.

Track playback rendering. Input: buffered aircraft positions across a simulated-time window and the playback cursor from op-008. Output: aircraft rendered at their interpolated position for the cursor, each with a trailing path over a configured lookback, with anomalous track segments visually distinct from nominal ones and anomaly zones appearing and clearing as their windows enter and leave the cursor. Constraints: interpolation is client-side between buffered frames, so motion is smooth independently of the poll interval; all map work stays inside the MapView boundary per map-001. Failure case: a track whose buffer has not yet loaded must hold its last known position and be marked stale, not jump to a default coordinate or vanish. Refs: FR-717, FR-718, US-A10, map-001, map-003, op-008, api-008.

Health endpoint. Input: GET /api/v1/health. Output: 200 with a JSON body reporting service status. Constraints: no database dependency, so it answers before persistence exists; every route is mounted under the /api/v1 prefix by a single APIRouter, so the prefix is declared once and no handler hard-codes it; the route is tagged system for OpenAPI grouping; the backend owns the full path, so neither the nginx proxy nor the Vite dev proxy rewrites or strips /api. Failure case: returning 200 while the app has failed to start, requiring a database connection to answer, or serving the endpoint at an unversioned path such as /health, fails the spec. Refs: FR-801, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.8, docs/qa.md section 16.

Operational picture endpoint. Input: GET /api/v1/operational-picture. Output: 200 with a payload whose shape matches frontend/src/types/operationalPicture.ts exactly: scenario, hypotheses, detectionSummary, rfSensors, aircraftTracks, timelineEvents. Constraints: field names and nesting mirror the TypeScript contract; confidence and severity values are Low|Medium|High strings; a contract test asserts shape parity in both directions. Amended 2026-09-04, three additions. (1) The two detection-summary fields become Low|Medium|High strings, and anomalyScore is renamed anomalyLevel because it is no longer a score. The contract as committed declared them numeric and the screen rendered '74.2%' and '0.92', which violates FR-715 and fails AC-11. This item is the last cheap moment to fix it: its own deliverable is a parity test whose purpose is to make the shape hard to change, so a shape frozen here is a shape defended afterwards. The mock's confidence value 'Medium Confidence' becomes 'Medium' for the same reason. Removing the percentage and toFixed rendering from the screen is part of this item; routing those values through a shared primitive is ui-001 and stays there. (2) What is actually served, given that four of the six sections have no producer. scenario comes from the most recent scenario run whose completed_at is set, falling back to the most recent run when none has completed (db-007). aircraftTracks are the latest position per aircraft within that run's final window -- 412 aircraft in the corpus as replayed -- with altitude converted from stored metres to the contract's feet, and name carrying the pseudonymised aircraft identifier, never a source one (dal-004). hypotheses, rfSensors and timelineEvents are empty arrays and detectionSummary is neutral, because no detector, RF source or generator exists. An empty section is honest; a populated one would be invented data reaching an analyst through a system whose argument is that this must not happen. (3) Reads go through a repository function rather than the handler (FR-904), which is what makes db-006's structural check assert over a real route rather than an empty set. Parity is proved by a backend test that parses the TypeScript contract and compares field sets in both directions, with frontend/ mounted read-only into the test container as compose.yaml and the Makefile already are; the test raises rather than skips when the mount is absent, because a skip here is the failure it exists to catch one level up (ops-003, adp-007). Failure case: adding, renaming, or dropping a field on either side without the other changing fails the contract test. A second: any percentage or decimal score in the payload fails the spec, and the parity test asserts the type of those two fields rather than only their names. A third: a real icao24 or callsign appearing in a track fails the spec. A fourth: serving a run that is not known to have completed while a completed run exists fails the spec. A fifth: the parity test skipping, rather than failing, when the frontend contract is not mounted. Refs: FR-802, FR-715, FR-904, AC-11, ui-001, api-003, db-006, db-007, dal-004, docs/implementation.md Phase 5.

Frontend data access via polling. Input: a poll interval and the backend base URL. Output: a single API module fetching /api/v1/operational-picture on an interval and handing the typed contract to the screen. Constraints: exactly one module performs the fetch; no WebSocket, EventSource, or push transport exists anywhere in the repo; on fetch failure the app falls back to the mock and surfaces a degraded-data indicator rather than blanking. Amended 2026-09-05, four additions. (1) Placement: src/lib/api.ts performs the fetch and nothing else does; src/hooks/useOperationalPicture.ts owns the interval, the fallback and the degraded flag; App.tsx stays the single seam and the screen keeps taking a typed prop, so no component learns where data comes from. (2) The interval defaults to 5000 ms, chosen by hand as NFR-503 requires rather than tuned, against the 0.40 s warm response measured for api-002. An interval shorter than the response time produces overlapping requests rather than fresher data, which is the specific way this gets got wrong. (3) The app reports itself degraded from first paint, before any response has arrived, because the mock it renders in that moment is example data and not the system's. The indicator clears on the first successful payload. On a failure after a success the last good payload is retained rather than replaced by the mock: stale real data behind a degraded indicator is more useful and more honest than reverting to invented data, and the mock stays the fallback only while nothing real has ever arrived. (4) The no-push-transport rule is checked in both suites, because neither container can see the whole repository: the frontend suite scans src/ and package.json, the backend suite scans app/ and pyproject.toml. The frontend check strips comments and string literals before matching, since parsing TypeScript would mean adding a dependency to a test; that is weaker than db-006's AST check and is mutation-tested both ways regardless, so a transport named in a comment does not fail and a real one does. Failure case: a 500 or network error clearing the operational picture, or any push transport appearing in the dependency tree, fails the spec. A second: a fetch issued from any module other than src/lib/api.ts fails the spec, since a second caller is how a screen quietly becomes coupled to the transport. A third: the degraded indicator absent while the mock is on screen fails the spec -- example data presented as though it were the system's is the failure this whole project argues against. Refs: FR-807, FR-718, US-E4, NFR-102, NFR-503, api-002, db-006, op-001.

Hypothesis read endpoints. Input: GET /api/v1/hypotheses and GET /api/v1/hypotheses/{id}. Output: a list of hypothesis summaries, and a full hypothesis with evidence, uncertainty, alternatives, generator, and status. Constraints: the detail payload includes the producing generator so the UI can satisfy ai-010; confidence is a Low|Medium|High string. Failure case: GET /api/v1/hypotheses/{unknown-id} must return 404 with a JSON error body, not 200 with null and not a 500. Refs: FR-804, FR-713, hyp-001, ai-010.

Analyst feedback endpoint. Input: POST /api/v1/hypotheses/{id}/feedback with a verdict of confirm, reject, needs-more-evidence, or false-positive, and an optional note. Output: 200 with the updated hypothesis status persisted. Constraints: verdict is validated against the enum before any write; status transitions follow New, Under review, Confirmed, Rejected, Inconclusive. Failure case: an unrecognised verdict returns 422 and leaves hypothesis status and the feedback table unchanged; an unknown hypothesis ID returns 404. Refs: FR-601, FR-602, FR-604, FR-805, fbk-001, fbk-002.

Scenario control endpoints. Input: POST /api/v1/scenario/start with scenario type, parameters, seed, and batch count; POST /api/v1/scenario/reset; GET /api/v1/scenario/runs. Output: a run record with its ID and status; a cleared run state; a list of recent runs with type, parameters, seed, and outcome. Constraints: start echoes back the seed actually used so a run is always reproducible from its record, including when the caller omitted one. Failure case: starting with an unknown scenario type returns 422 and creates no run row; reset while no run is active succeeds idempotently rather than erroring. Refs: FR-806, FR-201, FR-204, scn-001, scn-004. Amended 2026-09-13, before tests, after nav-001 made the screen reachable and scn-004 left its controls disabled. Four decisions. First, the scope narrows to two endpoints. POST /scenario/start and GET /scenario/runs are built; POST /scenario/reset is deferred to its own item and its control stays disabled with the reason on screen. The schema has no active-run concept -- a run is a row -- and db-007 records that nothing is ever deleted, so 'a cleared run state' has no honest meaning until a batch can be in flight and abandoned. Reset therefore belongs with cancellation rather than here. Inventing a destructive endpoint to fill the name, or a no-op one that returns 200 and changes nothing, are both worse than a control that says plainly it is not wired. Second, start returns 202 and the batch runs in the background while the screen polls. A batch is roughly 70 seconds and half a million rows, and the project has no task queue by scope. Blocking would make a 70-second request against an nginx whose default proxy read timeout is 60 seconds -- passing in development and failing in the container, which is the exact shape of defect this project keeps recording. A queued row with no worker to drain it ships a control that changes a row and produces no run, which is worse than the disabled button already on screen. A background task needs no dependency, and a process killed mid-batch leaves runs with a null completed_at, which db-007 already defines as not known to have finished rather than a new state to invent. The cost is that nothing can cancel a started batch; that is recorded rather than hidden, and it is why reset is deferred rather than dropped. Third, the response carries the base seed actually used and every seed derived from it. The constraint already on this item is that start echoes the seed so a run is reproducible from its record. With a background batch the response is the only thing the caller receives synchronously, so it carries the base seed -- drawn by the API when the caller omits one, never invented by the screen, which scn-004 settled -- and the per-run seeds, which a caller would otherwise have to wait for rows to discover. Fourth, a listed run carries its recorded parameters and ScenarioRunSummary does not gain them. The frontend contract's listed run is the summary's fields plus parameters, and replay cannot do without them. They are added on a listing model used by this endpoint alone rather than on ScenarioRunSummary, which api-002 also serves: the recorded parameters carry the incident's radius, elevation, offset and duration, and putting those on the operational picture would describe the staged incident to the analyst whose detectors are being measured against it. Ground truth is selected by neither. Failure cases added. A configuration whose incident begins at or after the run ends must be refused with 422 before any run row is opened: run_batch raises on it, but by then the request has returned 202 and the refusal survives only in a log, so the twenty mislabelled controls that guard exists for would be produced while the screen reported success. A run count outside the batch bounds must likewise be refused with 422 and open no run row. Start returning 200 with a completed batch summary fails the spec, because it would mean the request blocked. A listed run carrying ground truth, or ScenarioRunSummary gaining a parameters field, fails the spec and api-009. The route constructing the engine, the layout or the corpus window itself fails the spec: the batch launcher is injected, so the endpoint is testable without a corpus on disk or a database, and FR-904 keeps SQL out of handlers. Scope: two route handlers, a listing model, a repository function that lists runs, an injected batch launcher with one real implementation and a seam for tests, and the router registration. It wires no screen -- the frontend swapping its fixture for a fetch is a separate step, and until it happens the note on that screen still says the rows are a fixture. Refs adds: db-007, api-002, api-009, nav-001, scn-003, FR-904, NFR-503. Defect found 2026-09-13 by running it, after api-010 put the button on screen. The launcher called Pseudonymiser.from_environment directly, and inside the container the pseudonymisation seed arrives from compose as an empty string rather than as absent, so every batch died immediately with 'PSEUDONYM_SEED is not set' while the screen reported the batch accepted. The command-line entrypoints do not have this fault: both clear a present-but-empty variable and then read backend/.env, each with a comment explaining the trap. There were therefore two copies of the remedy and the launcher was a third site that needed it and did not have it, which is why the fix extracts the remedy into one function that all three call rather than adding a third copy. This is the third recurrence of the present-but-empty defect recorded in this project (adp-007 first, then the container's own environment) and the second recurrence of the more general one: the place the code runs is not the place the tests describe. The launcher's existing tests could not have caught it, because they substitute the pseudonymiser to avoid needing a seed at all. Added failure case: a batch launched in a process whose seed variable is present but empty must read the seed from the env file and run, rather than raising where only a log can see it. Recorded limitation, not fixed here: a batch that fails after acceptance is invisible to the analyst, because the response has already been sent and nothing writes the failure anywhere the screen reads. That needs its own item.

Server-side view filtering. Input: GET /api/v1/operational-picture with a view parameter of anomalous, nominal, or all. Output: a payload containing only the matching rfSensors, aircraftTracks, and timelineEvents, plus metadata carrying the suppressed count per collection. Constraints: filtering happens in the query, not by returning everything and discarding client-side, so the payload shrinks with the selection; the suppressed counts are what keep op-004's hidden footer truthful once rows stop arriving. Failure case: an unrecognised view value must return 422 rather than silently defaulting to all, and a filtered response omitting the suppressed-count metadata fails the spec. Refs: FR-809, FR-716, api-002, op-004, op-007.

Time-windowed track query for playback buffering. Input: a scenario run ID and a simulated-time span. Output: aircraft positions across that span, ordered by time per aircraft, sufficient for the frontend to interpolate between frames. Constraints: the frontend buffers ahead of the cursor and issues one request per span rather than one per frame, so the request rate is decoupled from the frame rate per FR-718; the span is bounded server-side to cap payload size. Failure case: a requested span exceeding the bound must be rejected or truncated with the truncation reported, never silently served in full; a span outside the run's recorded window must return an empty series, not an error. Refs: FR-810, FR-718, US-A10, op-008, map-004, adp-001.

Ground truth is never exposed outside the evaluation harness. Input: any API response, canonical observation, anomaly, evidence bundle, or hypothesis. Output: none of them carry the injected ground truth for the run. Constraints: the generator records what it injected on scenario_runs.ground_truth and that column is read by the evaluation harness only; no adapter, DAL record, detector input, API response, or evidence bundle may carry it, whether as a field, a label, or an inferable artefact such as a scenario-type string on an observation; GET /api/v1/scenario/runs may report that a run has ground truth recorded but never its content while the run is scorable. Failure case: an /api/v1/operational-picture or /api/v1/anomalies response including the scenario type or the injected event for the active run fails the spec, because a detector or an analyst able to see the answer invalidates every metric computed from that run. Refs: FR-207, FR-806, NFR-604, US-R5, AC-04, scn-002, adp-002, evb-001, eval-002.

Core schema and migrations. Input: an empty PostgreSQL database, reachable through the Engine db-005 constructs. Output: alembic added to pyproject.toml and locked; tables observations, quarantined_records, anomalies, evidence_bundles, hypotheses, analyst_feedback and scenario_runs created by ordered Alembic revisions; geometry(Point,4326) on observations.location and geometry(Polygon,4326) on anomalies.affected_area, both GiST-indexed; NOT NULL on observations over the provenance fields dal-003 requires (scenario_run_id, data_mode, source_id, source_type), and NOT NULL on quarantined_records over scenario_run_id, field and reason, with source_id, source_type and observation_type nullable there because dal-002 states attribution is best-effort -- a record can fail precisely because it lacks the field that identifies it. Constraints: Alembic is the documented migration convention, with revisions written by hand and autogenerate disabled, because autogenerate does not understand PostGIS geometry columns and would emit a revision nobody has read; the convention and the command that applies it are documented in README.md and exposed as a root Makefile target (ops-003); migrations apply cleanly from empty; source-specific fields live in the observation payload as JSONB, so the canonical table stays stable as sources are added; the hypotheses table carries generator, model_id, generation_params and raw_response from this first revision rather than a later one, because raw_response is not retrofittable after a campaign has run (db-002); spatial columns are stored as geometry and cast to geography at query time, so db-004's distance is computed by PostGIS rather than by the application while the full geometry function set stays available to the Phase 6 spatial clustering; this item creates schema only -- no repository implementation, which is db-003's, so that a red test can distinguish a wrong column type from a wrong write. Tests run against a disposable database in the postgis Compose service, carry a database marker, and read TEST_DATABASE_URL rather than DATABASE_URL, skipping when it is absent, so db-005's guarantee that unit tests need no live database survives; the coverage gate omits modules requiring a live database exactly when those tests skip, so the 90 per cent gate is measured over what was actually exercisable, and the containerised run -- the only one with a database -- remains the authoritative number. Failure case: applying migrations twice from empty errors. A second failure case: a missing PostGIS extension is not reported at migration time and surfaces later as type geography does not exist at first query, which is the failure scripts/smoke-test.sh already guards for the container and this item guards for the schema. A third failure case: the schema accepts an observation with a null scenario_run_id, data_mode, source_id or source_type, which is the half of dal-003 that item defers to here, and the same for dal-002's quarantine attribution. A fourth failure case: hypotheses created without the four reproducibility columns, which passes every test that exists today because nothing writes to that table yet, and is discovered only after a campaign has run. A fifth failure case: a module omitted from the coverage gate in both the native and the containerised run, so it is measured nowhere -- the omission must be conditional on database availability rather than unconditional, otherwise the exclusion that keeps the native gate honest becomes the hole that hides an untested repository. Amended 2026-08-29, before tests were written, on two counts that the item's own text got wrong. First, a seventh table: the six named here and in docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 9 have nowhere to put a QuarantineRecord, whose shape is (source_id?, source_type?, scenario_run_id, observation_type?, field, reason) and carries no timestamp, no location and no payload, because those are what failed validation. Storing it in observations would require those three columns to become nullable, which would remove the NOT NULL guarantee dal-003 defers to this item -- so the item would delete the assertion it exists to add. The ERD in section 9 predates dal-002 and has been amended to match. Second, the skip signal: this text said database tests skip when DATABASE_URL is absent, which was true when written and was falsified a day later by tests/conftest.py, which sets DATABASE_URL for every test so that db-005's engine tests have a value that resolves but does not connect. It is therefore never absent. A separate TEST_DATABASE_URL is the signal instead, which is also a safety boundary rather than only a naming choice: this item's tests create and drop schema, and keying them on whatever DATABASE_URL happens to hold would eventually run a DROP against a development database. Refs: FR-901, FR-902, FR-906, dal-002, dal-003, db-002, db-003, db-004, db-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 9, docs/qa.md section 34.

Hypothesis persistence and reproducibility. Input: a generation result from any arm (ai-003's envelope) and the identity of the evidence bundle it explains. Output: one stored row carrying the whole ai-001 hypothesis plus generator (template|local|hosted), model_id, generation_params and verbatim raw_response. Constraints: the four reproducibility columns exist from the first migration and do -- what 0001 could not know is the field vocabulary ai-001 later settled, so title, uncertainty and alternatives are RENAMED to hypothesis_title, evidence_against_or_uncertainty and alternative_explanations rather than mapped, because a mapping layer is a permanent place for two vocabularies to drift silently and the table holds zero rows, so the rename is free today and never again; summary and recommended_human_action have no column at all and gain one, which is the same class of defect as a late raw_response and has the same remedy cost after a campaign; grounding_passed becomes THREE-VALUED -- passed, failed, not yet checked -- because a hypothesis is written before ai-008 runs and a two-valued flag makes 'failed the check' and 'was never checked' identical, which is the typed-absence failure evb-001 exists to prevent and this repository has recorded three times; status gains the check constraint its neighbours generator and confidence already carry, over FR-602's five review states, and a new row starts at New; reading a stored bundle must yield its identity, since a hypothesis references one by id and evb-002's reader exposes none today, which is a blocker found by attempting the write rather than by reading the schema. model_id is a dated identifier and never a moving alias; raw_response is verbatim pre-parse output and never the parsed hypothesis re-serialised, because the difference only surfaces when somebody investigates a grounding failure months later and finds a record of what was understood rather than of what was said. The write goes through the repository, never SQL in a caller (FR-904). Failure cases: writing a model-arm row with model_id or raw_response null is rejected at the repository boundary -- a SECOND guard, ai-003 having already made such a result unconstructible, kept because this is the failure nobody can repair after a campaign and a boundary check holds against a row assembled some other way; a template row carrying a model id is rejected in the other direction; an unknown review status is refused by the database rather than stored. Refs: FR-508, FR-602, FR-903, FR-904, NFR-602, US-R3, US-R4, AC-06, ai-001, ai-002, ai-003, ai-008, db-007, evb-002, docs/phase9_hypothesis_layer.md section 10. Amended 2026-09-27, two additions found by building the campaign that would consume this (ai-012), both in the class this item already calls the failure nobody can repair afterwards. (1) THE THREE-VALUED GROUNDING COLUMN HAS NO WRITER FOR TWO OF ITS THREE VALUES. save_hypothesis hard-codes 'not yet checked' and nothing updates it afterwards, so every row a campaign wrote would carry a verdict the campaign had in hand and never stored -- the typed absence built correctly and then never filled, which is worse than the two-valued flag it was built to avoid, because the column now looks capable of the distinction while the data never makes it. A repository function therefore records the verdict against one row id, taking ai-008's report rather than a bool so that 'flagged' and 'the check itself failed' cannot arrive as the same value; it refuses an unknown row id rather than silently affecting nothing, since a verdict written to no row is indistinguishable from a verdict written, and it refuses a move back to not-checked, because 'we looked and then stopped having looked' is not an event. (2) THE ROW CANNOT SAY WHICH ARM WAS ASKED, only which generator answered, and the campaign is the first caller where the two differ. When the model arm falls back, the stored template row is byte-identical to the template baseline's own row for the same bundle: a fallback is then invisible in the data, eval-005's per-arm counts are ambiguous at exactly the rows that matter most, and ai-010's screen indicator -- a fallback hypothesis must be visibly distinguishable from a primary-arm one -- is unbuildable on this schema rather than merely unbuilt. requested_generator is added NOT NULL over the same vocabulary and check constraint as generator, and generator != requested_generator is the DEFINITION of a fallback rather than a state to be refused, since ai-007 goes model-to-template and ai-006 goes hosted-to-local. The table holds zero rows -- nothing in app/ has ever written one -- which is the same free-today-and-never-again window the renames above used, and this is the second and last use of it. Failure cases added: a campaign row that does not say which arm was asked fails the spec; a grounding verdict recorded against a row id that does not exist is refused rather than counted as written. Refs adds: ai-010, ai-012.

PostGIS implementation of the DAL's repository port, the item that tests whether the port survived contact with a real database. Input: the ObservationRepository Protocol defined by dal-002, and canonical observations plus quarantine records produced by ingest_batch against the schema db-001 created. Output: a PostgreSQL/PostGIS implementation of that Protocol living in a repository module; a replayed window persists to observations and quarantined_records and is readable back; GeoAlchemy2 added to pyproject.toml and locked, and the geometry filterwarnings entry removed from pyproject.toml at the same time. Constraints: the Protocol's signature is the contract under test -- no storage-engine type may be added to it to make the implementation fit, so Location stays two floats and the WKB/ST_SetSRID conversion happens inside the repository; save_batch is one database transaction, so a failure part-way through leaves neither collection written; no caller-supplied primary key; all SQL and all spatial logic live here and nowhere else (FR-904, first half). The in-memory fake in tests/fakes.py is retained rather than replaced -- two implementations of one port is what makes the port meaningful, and it keeps the unit tier runnable with no Docker. No coverage omission: measured, the module sits at 53 per cent natively and the suite at 97.44 per cent, comfortably over the gate, and a 53 per cent reading is the honest signal that this module was not exercised here -- omitting it would make the native figure less informative rather than more. The containerised run remains authoritative and reports it at 100 per cent. Failure case: a batch of ten with three invalid must leave seven rows in observations and three in quarantined_records, and an induced failure between the two writes must leave zero of both -- seven observations with no quarantine trace fails the spec. A second failure case: an observation whose location round-trips to different coordinates, or is stored with an SRID other than 4326, fails the spec. A third: any change to the Protocol signature that introduces a session, an ORM model, a WKT or WKB string, or a caller-supplied identifier fails the spec, and if the implementation cannot be written without one, that is the finding and it is recorded in thesis_notes.md against the standing prediction (geometry and atomicity are the risks, identity is not) rather than worked around. Refs: FR-904, FR-901, US-E2, AC-02, dal-002, dal-003, db-001, db-005, db-004, db-006, docs/qa.md section 39.

PostGIS spatial query, the justification for the spatial database. Input: an RF anomaly zone geometry, a radius N in kilometres, and a time window. Output: the set of track discontinuities whose location falls within N km of the zone inside that window. Constraints: distance computed by PostGIS on geography, not by application-side arithmetic; the radius is a parameter, not a constant. Failure case: a discontinuity just outside N km must be excluded, and an empty result set must return an empty list rather than null or an error. Refs: FR-905, FR-305, anom-004, anom-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 9. Amended 2026-09-15, before tests, on picking it up. Four things settled. First, this item is the proximity query and not the clustering one. FR-905 names 'track discontinuities within N km of an RF anomaly zone' and this item's own text describes exactly that, so the requirement and the item already agree. What disagrees is anom-004, whose text says its clusters are 'computed by the PostGIS query in db-004', and db-001's comment on the anomalies GiST index, which calls db-004 'the clustering query'. Two references to a query this item does not describe, neither noticed until now -- the same shape as FR-304 having no item at all, and found the same way, by reading the items rather than the phase heading. Second, clustering becomes db-009 rather than a note. It is real work that something must own, and leaving a needed capability described only in prose is exactly what FR-304 cost earlier in this phase; the correction is made by writing the item, not by recording that one is wanted. anom-004's reference is corrected when that item is picked up, and db-001's comment is left as it stands -- the revision is applied and its behaviour is right, so the comment is noted here rather than edited there. Third, the table read is detection_findings and not anomalies. db-008 created it because anomalies describes the reportable kind -- it requires a severity, a Polygon affected_area and a bundle link, none of which an intermediate finding has -- and it carries the GiST index on a Point location that this query is the reason for. Fourth, the input is any geometry with a radius rather than a polygon specifically. ST_DWithin on geography accepts either, and today the only producer of an RF zone is anom-001, which emits a point per sensor because an area needs corroboration from more than one; polygons arrive once db-009 clusters them. Requiring a polygon now would mean inventing one from a point, which is the coverage footprint this project has never modelled. Failure cases added. The boundary is bracketed rather than pinned at exact equality, and the reason is a measurement that contradicted this item as first amended. It claimed ST_DWithin is inclusive, so a finding exactly N km away would be inside; measured against PostGIS 3.5 on 2026-09-15, it is not. ST_Distance between two points returns 34338.94037894 m and ST_DWithin at exactly that value returns false, with no floating-point drift in the round trip through kilometres -- the operator itself excludes the boundary on geography. That was asserted here from documentation rather than from the database, which is the error this project keeps finding in its own reasoning. The specified behaviour is therefore that a finding one metre inside the radius is returned and one metre outside is not, which brackets the edge to metre precision without depending on an exact-equality semantics no real input ever occupies; exact equality is recorded as undefined and left to PostGIS. A query that computes distance on geometry rather than geography fails the spec, because degrees are not metres and the error varies with latitude -- at 52 degrees north a degree of longitude is about 69 km and a degree of latitude about 111 km, so a radius expressed in degrees is wrong by a different factor in each direction. Findings belonging to another scenario run must never be returned, whatever their location: every metric in eval-002 is computed per run, and a query that reaches across runs would silently fuse evidence from two different staged incidents. Refs adds: db-008, db-009, anom-001, eval-002. Further failure case, added 2026-09-15 while building: a radius of zero or less is refused rather than answered. It would otherwise return an empty result that is indistinguishable from 'nothing nearby', which is the silent wrong answer this project guards against everywhere else -- and unlike an empty result, it is always a caller error.

Database connectivity: engine, session, and configuration. Input: DATABASE_URL in the environment, in the form compose already passes to the backend and pipeline services. Output: sqlalchemy and psycopg added to pyproject.toml and locked; a single SQLAlchemy 2.x Engine created once during application startup and disposed on shutdown via the lifespan hook; a sessionmaker bound to it; and a FastAPI dependency yielding one Session per request that rolls back on exception and closes on completion. Constraints: the driver is psycopg 3, addressed as postgresql+psycopg://; the URL is read from the environment only, with no DSN, host, or credential literal in application source or in a fixture (NFR-401); exactly one Engine exists per process, so the connection pool is shared rather than rebuilt per request; engine construction is lazy and opens no connection, so unit tests need no live database and the live connectivity check stays in scripts/smoke-test.sh; GET /api/v1/health continues to answer without acquiring a connection, preserving api-001 so a degraded database cannot present as an unreachable service. Failure case: a missing or empty DATABASE_URL must fail loudly at startup rather than at first query; constructing an Engine inside a request handler fails the spec; and a request whose handler raises must leave no session open and no transaction uncommitted. Refs: FR-901, FR-904, NFR-401, api-001, db-001, db-003, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 10, docs/qa.md section 18.

Route handlers hold no SQL, no session construction, and no spatial logic, the enforcement half of FR-904. Input: the route modules under app/api/. Output: a structural test asserting that no route module constructs a session, builds an Engine, issues SQL, or calls a PostGIS function; handlers obtain data only by calling a repository function. Constraints: the check parses the modules rather than matching source text, because a substring match is satisfied by an example in a docstring -- the defect that made an earlier absence test pass vacuously (docs/qa.md section 38, db-001). This item is split from db-003 deliberately: db-003 is the repository existing and being correct, this is nothing bypassing it, and the two fail at different times -- a broken repository fails at write time against a populated database, a leaked query fails review and nothing else. It cannot be proved before there is a data-serving route, so it lands with api-002 in Phase 5, not with db-003. Failure case: a raw SELECT, a session or Engine constructed in a handler, or a PostGIS function called from a route module fails the spec. A second failure case: the test passing against a handler that contains a violation written inside a comment or docstring means the check is matching text and fails the spec itself -- it is mutation-tested both ways before this item is set passing. Refs: FR-904, US-E2, db-003, api-002, docs/qa.md sections 38 and 39.

Scenario run completion, so a partial run is distinguishable from a finished one. Input: a scenario run created by any producer -- adp-007's replay today, scn-001's generator later -- and its outcome. Output: a second Alembic revision adding completed_at, a nullable timestamptz, to scenario_runs; a repository function that sets it; and replay setting it after its final batch has committed. A run whose completed_at is null is a run not known to have finished. Constraints: nullable with no server default and no backfill, because the column's whole meaning is that absence is informative -- a default would mark every existing row complete including the partial ones this item exists to find. Set after the last batch commits, never before and never in the same transaction as the first, since a flag written up front records an intention rather than an outcome. Nothing is deleted on failure: the rows a partial run wrote are kept, because they are evidence about what went wrong and a cascading delete over 133,634 observations is a surprising thing for a failure path to do. Three states -- running, failed, crashed -- are deliberately collapsed into one, because a process killed outright cannot record its own failure, so a status column with a 'failed' value would be reliable for caught exceptions and silently wrong for everything else; null honestly means 'not known to have completed'. Written as db-007 rather than folded into adp-007 or scn-001 because the column belongs to the schema and every producer of a run must set it, so it cannot live inside one producer. Why this exists: adp-007 chose one window as the unit of work rather than one run, so an interrupted replay leaves its committed batches in place. Combined with a new run being created on every invocation rather than resuming, the database accumulates partial runs that are indistinguishable from complete ones by inspection. Harmless while nothing reads runs; wrong the moment eval-001 counts them or a detector reads a window from one. Failure case: a replay that raises part-way through must leave completed_at null on its run, and must leave the batches it already wrote in place -- deleting them, or marking the run complete, both fail the spec. A second failure case: completed_at set before the final batch commits fails the spec, and is tested by observing the run's completed_at from inside the last save_batch and asserting it is still null. A third: the revision applied to a database holding rows must leave every existing completed_at null rather than backfilling it, since those rows are exactly the runs whose completion is unknown. A fourth: applying the revision twice from empty must not error, and downgrading must drop the column. A fifth failure case: completing a run id that is absent from scenario_runs must raise rather than update nothing, because an UPDATE matching no rows reports success over a run that was never marked, which is the silent completion this column exists to make impossible. Refs: FR-201, US-E1, AC-01, db-001, db-003, adp-007, scn-001, scn-003, eval-001, api-006, docs/qa.md section 40.

Detection finding persistence. Input: the findings one rule produced for one scenario run -- anom-001's RF deviation episodes or anom-010's track discontinuities -- with the run id and the rule that produced them. Output: rows in a detection_findings table carrying the run, the rule, the finding type, the subject the finding concerns, its simulated-time window, a Point location and the triggering readings as recorded references; plus a read-back returning the same models that went in. Constraints: every finding carries the run it belongs to, because eval-002 computes every metric per run against that run's recorded ground truth and a finding that cannot name its run cannot be scored; the location is a geometry column with a GiST index, because db-004 and anom-004 are spatial queries over exactly this table and an unindexed one fails as a performance claim rather than a correctness one, which is the kind of defect that survives every functional test; the write is per run per rule and replaces what was there, so re-running detection after a rule changes cannot leave a stale set behind to be counted twice; all SQL stays in the storage layer and nothing above it learns a storage type (FR-904). Failure cases: a finding naming a run that does not exist must be refused by the database rather than stored orphaned; a finding whose window ends before it begins must be refused; reading findings for a run that has none must return an empty list rather than null or an error; a second write of the same rule's findings for the same run must leave the count unchanged rather than doubling it. Refs: FR-905, FR-904, NFR-601, db-001, db-003, db-007, anom-001, anom-010, anom-004, anom-005, db-004, evb-002, eval-002. Written 2026-09-14, on picking up db-004 and finding it had nothing to query: the anomalies table exists, no code writes to it or reads it, and no item covered doing so. Five decisions. First, findings are stored in their own table rather than in anomalies. That table describes the reportable kind -- it requires a severity, requires a Polygon affected_area, and links to an evidence bundle. The two rules built so far produce neither a severity nor an area: anom-008's amendment made the first deliberate, and anom-001's ninth decision made the second, because an area needs corroboration from more than one source and inventing a radius would mean modelling a coverage footprint the project has never measured. Forcing findings into that table would mean three nullable columns and a polygon that misstates what was observed. Second, anomalies gains a scenario_run_id in the same migration. It has none today, so no anomaly can say which run produced it, and every metric in eval-002 is computed per run. That is a gap in db-001 rather than a change of design, and it costs nothing now and a data migration after a campaign. Third, one canonical finding shape whatever rule produced it. The detectors return different models -- an RF episode carries a cell and a peak deviation, a track discontinuity carries an aircraft and a shape -- and a storage layer knowing about both would gain a branch per rule, which is exactly the dependency dal-001 removed one layer down. The same argument holds here: one shape every rule becomes, with whatever is rule-specific carried in a details payload, so a third detector needs no change to the storage layer at all. This is the RQ1 extensibility claim made at a second seam, and it is worth measuring when anom-003 lands. Fourth, the write replaces rather than appends. Detection is deterministic and regenerable from the run's seed, so a finding is derived rather than historical, and db-007's rule that nothing is ever deleted does not reach it -- that rule is about runs, which are facts about what happened. Appending would be worse than deleting: after a rule changes, the old findings and the new sit together and every metric counts both, silently. Fifth, the location is a Point and the index is GiST, following db-001, whose comment on the anomalies geometry index names db-004 as its reason. The discontinuities db-004 and anom-004 query live in this table, so the index belongs here too. Scope: one migration adding the table, its index and its constraints plus the anomalies column; one canonical finding model with converters from each rule's output; and one storage module with a write and a read. It computes no distances and groups nothing -- db-004 and anom-004 are the queries and they are separate items. Recorded and deliberately not resolved here: db-004 and anom-004 describe different queries, db-004 a proximity test against a zone geometry and anom-004 a clustering of findings among themselves, while db-001's own comment calls db-004 the clustering query. Both queries are wanted. Which item owns which is settled when db-004 is picked up; this item provides the table they both read. Amended 2026-09-19, on the evb-002 traceability measurement. from_track_gap wrote the finding's window ends into evidence_refs, which is right for one of anom-010's two mechanisms and wrong for the other. evidence_refs is a citation field, and a citation must name a row: it therefore takes its timestamps from anom-010's new observed_at rather than from the window. The failure case is the measured one -- a frozen_position finding whose refs cite started_at resolves to zero rows and fails evb-002's build, 91 times in 1,021 citations. This is a change to what is written and not to the shape, so no column moves and no migration is owed: findings are derived and regenerable under this item's own replace-rather-than-append rule, and the stored corpus catches up the next time a rule runs. No figure measured before this date is threatened by it, because nothing read evidence_refs until evb-002 did. from_track_cluster is deliberately left alone and recorded here as a known non-resolver: its refs are {aircraft_id} with no timestamp at all, which as a coordinate matches every report that aircraft made rather than one, and anom-004 clusters are not reportable so no bundle cites them -- evb-002 must refuse that shape by name rather than match it loosely. Refs adds: evb-002, anom-004, anom-010.

PostGIS clustering of detection findings. Input: the findings of one scenario run for one rule, a cluster radius in kilometres, and a time window. Output: groups of findings that lie within the radius of one another, each with a representative centroid and a geometry covering its members, returned as an ordered, deterministic set. Constraints: grouping is performed by PostGIS on geography rather than by application-side arithmetic, for the reason db-004 gives -- degrees are not metres and the error varies with latitude; the radius is a parameter, not a constant; the same findings and radius always give the same groups, including the order they are returned in, because a run must be reproducible from its seed (NFR-601); a finding belongs to exactly one group. Failure cases: two findings separated by more than the radius, with nothing between them, must not be reported as one group; a single isolated finding must be returned as a group of one rather than dropped, because anom-006 needs to know a dropout happened alone; an empty input must return an empty list rather than null or an error; and groups whose member order depends on the order rows came back from the database fail the spec. Refs: FR-301, FR-305, FR-904, NFR-601, db-004, db-008, anom-004, anom-005, anom-006, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 9. Written 2026-09-15, splitting the clustering half out of db-004 on picking that item up. db-004 is the proximity query FR-905 names and its text describes; anom-004 and db-001 both refer to it as the clustering query, which it never was. Two decisions. First, the function is ST_ClusterWithin and not ST_ClusterDBSCAN. Scope v2 cut DBSCAN, and while the PostGIS implementation is a spatial function rather than a learned model, using it would put a method the scope names as excluded into the detection path and would need a minimum-points parameter that nothing in the project has a basis for choosing. ST_ClusterWithin is transitive-closure grouping on a single distance: deterministic, one parameter, and explainable in a sentence to an analyst, which is what this phase is for. Second, the transitive property is recorded as a limitation rather than discovered as a defect. Grouping by transitive closure means a chain of findings each within the radius of the next forms one group however far the chain runs, so a cluster can span far more than the radius that produced it. That is the correct behaviour for a spreading interference zone and the wrong behaviour for a line of aircraft on a single airway, and the project has no basis yet for preferring either. The measurement that would settle it -- whether the roughly 138 background discontinuities in a quiet run ever chain into a group large enough for anom-006 to raise a data-source issue on -- is owed as soon as this item and anom-004 exist, and is the open risk recorded when anom-010 landed. Amended 2026-09-15, before tests, on picking it up. Four things the item assumed turn out not to hold, all four found by asking the database rather than the documentation -- the error this project has now made twice, most recently in db-004's boundary case. First, ST_ClusterWithin has no geography variant. Both overloads in PostGIS 3.5's function catalogue take geometry and a plain double, and that distance is in the SRID's own units, which for 4326 is degrees. The constraint as written -- grouping performed on geography -- is therefore not satisfiable with the function this item chose, and the two halves of the item contradicted each other from the moment it was written. It is resolved by projecting to EPSG:3035, ETRS89-extended LAEA Europe, an equal-area metre projection covering the whole corpus box, clustering there, rather than by changing function. The substance of the constraint survives: the radius means metres and the database measures it. What changes is the mechanism named. Measured against PostGIS 3.5 on 2026-09-15 at the box corners and centre, a 5 km separation in LAEA differs from the geodesic distance on geography by at most 2.57 m, or 0.055 per cent, worst at 54 north 3 east; the alternative the constraint was written to forbid, a radius applied to raw degrees, is wrong by about 62 per cent between the two axes at 52 north. Three orders of magnitude separate the approximation accepted from the one rejected, which is what makes the amendment honest rather than convenient. The alternative that would satisfy the constraint literally -- a recursive transitive closure over ST_DWithin on geography -- was rejected: it is exact, and it buys 2.57 m of accuracy on a radius nothing in the project has a basis for choosing to within a kilometre, at the cost of the property this item selected ST_ClusterWithin for, which is being explainable to an analyst in one sentence. Second, the window variant is used and not the aggregate. ST_ClusterWithin returns an array of geometry collections and so loses row identity: every finding would have to be joined back to the collection containing it to learn which group it landed in. ST_ClusterWithinWin, verified present in PostGIS 3.5 and confirmed to chain transitively across a three-point chain at 5 km, returns a cluster id per row. Third, the cluster ids the database produces are never the order the groups come back in. ST_ClusterWithinWin numbers groups in its own internal order over rows that have no guaranteed order unless one is imposed, which is precisely the failure case this item already names. Ordering is derived from content instead: members within a group by started_at, then subject, then id; groups by their first member's key once sorted. Fourth, the centroid is computed in metres and the covering geometry in degrees, and the split is measured rather than tidy. A centroid taken in degrees is the arithmetic mean of coordinates, which underweights longitude because a degree of it is shorter; for a cluster spanning about 25 km at 52 north the two centroids lie 7.69 m apart, and the metre-space one is the correct areal centre. The covering geometry is computed in 4326 because its vertices are findings that are already stored exactly, and a round trip through 3035 does not return them unchanged -- longitude 5.0 comes back as 4.999999999999997 and latitude 52.0 as 52.000000000000014. The rule behind both is one rule: each value is computed in the space where that value is right. Two further failure cases. A radius of zero or less is refused rather than answered, for the reason db-004 gives -- an empty result would be indistinguishable from nothing clustering. And the covering geometry of a group of one is a point and of a group of two a line, not a polygon; that is recorded here rather than papered over, because a group of one has no observed extent and inventing a polygon would claim an area nothing was seen across. The anomalies table's Polygon affected_area is anom-004's problem to solve when it promotes a cluster to a reportable anomaly, not this query's. Refs adds: db-001, NFR-601.

Canonical observation model and required-field validation. Input: a source-specific record emitted by any adapter. Output: a canonical observation with source_id, source_type, observation_type, timestamp, location, data_mode, validation_status, provenance, and a typed payload. Constraints: one model for every source; payload typing is per observation type via Pydantic; validation runs before persistence. Failure case: a record missing timestamp or location must not produce a canonical observation and must route to quarantine per dal-002. Amended 2026-08-25: TrackPayload gains contact_staleness_s alongside position_staleness_s. The two are different measurements, and the distinction is a detection discriminator rather than a detail. Position staleness is time minus lastposupdate, the age of the coordinate carried inside a row; contact staleness is time minus lastcontact, the interval since any message was received from the aircraft. A row where both are stale means the aircraft is no longer heard from at all, which is scenario type 4's coverage gap. A row with fresh contact and a stale position means the aircraft is still transmitting while its position has stopped advancing, which is scenario type 2's GNSS degradation signature. Without the second field the canonical model cannot represent the difference, and the two scenario types are indistinguishable in the data the detectors read -- a confound built into the model rather than discovered in the results. The signal is present in quantity: 4,553 positioned rows of the current extract, 3.4 per cent, carry a position more than ten seconds older than their last contact, to a maximum of 1,552 seconds, and the distributions confirm the mechanism rather than merely suggesting it, since contact staleness caps at 299.97 seconds where OpenSky drops a state vector after roughly five minutes of silence while position staleness runs on to 1,561 seconds. The field is required rather than optional because lastcontact is present on every one of the extract's 133,634 rows, including all 500 null-position rows, so requiring it creates no quarantine that a null position does not already cause; position_staleness_s by contrast is absent on exactly those 500. This item returns to passes false until the added field is proven, because the description now claims a shape the model does not yet have. A second failure case: deriving contact staleness from lastposupdate, or position staleness from lastcontact, which silently collapses the discriminator and makes scenario types 2 and 4 look alike in every downstream rule. Refs: FR-101, FR-102, US-E2, dal-002, dal-003.

Quarantine of malformed records. Input: a batch of records where some fail required-field validation. Output: valid records persisted as canonical observations; invalid records persisted to quarantine with the failing field, the reason, and the source attribution; a per-run count of each. Constraints: nothing is silently dropped; no invalid record aborts the ingest run; persistence happens through a repository port -- an interface accepting canonical observations and quarantine records, with the storage engine behind it -- so this item is provable against an in-memory implementation and the PostGIS implementation lands with db-003, which requires that seam regardless of build order; the two writes are one unit of work, so a run that persists observations and then fails before writing quarantine records must leave neither. What this item proves is DAL behaviour, not database enforcement: the NOT NULL and foreign-key guarantees over the same fields are db-001's to prove, and passes: true here asserts the first claim only. Failure case: a batch of ten records with three invalid must persist seven observations and three quarantine rows and complete without raising; raising, or persisting seven with no quarantine trace, fails the spec. A second failure case: a port signature carrying a storage-engine type -- a WKT or WKB string, a session, an ORM model, a database-assigned identifier the caller is expected to supply -- fails the spec, because the DAL would then know about PostGIS and the seam db-003 exists to enforce would already be broken. Refs: FR-103, NFR-102, US-E3, AC-02, dal-001, dal-003, db-001, db-003, docs/qa.md section 26.

Provenance on every accepted record. Input: a validated record and its ingest context. Output: a canonical observation carrying source ID, source type, data mode, and scenario run ID. Constraints: provenance is attached at the DAL, not per adapter, so it cannot be forgotten by a new adapter; data_mode distinguishes replayed from synthetic. The guarantee is asserted twice, at different layers and at different times: the DAL must refuse to construct a record with provenance missing, which is what this item proves, and the schema must refuse to store one, which is db-001's NOT NULL constraints and is proven there. Marking this item passing therefore asserts the DAL half only, and the constraint half is outstanding until db-001 lands. Failure case: a canonical observation constructed with a null scenario run ID or an absent data mode fails the spec. A second failure case: provenance applied inside an adapter rather than at the DAL passes its own tests while leaving the next adapter free to omit it, which is the failure this item exists to prevent and is asserted by driving two different adapters through the same DAL entrypoint. Refs: FR-104, US-A7, US-E2, AC-02, dal-001, dal-002, db-001, adp-003, docs/qa.md section 26.

Aircraft identifier pseudonymisation at the DAL. Input: a source record carrying source-native aircraft identifiers (icao24 and callsign for the OpenSky adapter) and a pseudonymisation seed held as fixed project configuration outside the repository. Output: a canonical observation in which those identifiers are replaced by deterministic pseudonyms -- aircraft_id derived from icao24, flight_id from callsign -- with the source values discarded rather than retained alongside. A blank or absent callsign yields no flight_id rather than a pseudonym of the empty string, since OpenSky reports many of them and an empty callsign is missing data rather than an identity. Constraints: the substitution happens at the DAL, not per adapter, so a new adapter cannot forget it -- the same argument dal-003 makes for provenance, and enforced the same way, by refusing a payload that arrives with aircraft_id or flight_id already populated; the pseudonym is a deterministic function of the source identifier and the configured seed, so one aircraft maps to one pseudonym within and across runs and track continuity survives for the detectors; the two identifier namespaces are separated in the derivation, so an icao24 and a callsign that happen to share text cannot collide; no reverse mapping is persisted anywhere the application can read, so a pseudonym cannot be resolved back from the database or an API response; the pseudonym carries no source information, so airline prefixes encoded in a callsign and country blocks encoded in an icao24 allocation do not survive into it; the real identifiers remain in the local extract, which the licence permits, since the restriction is on publication and disclosure rather than on local use. The seed is separate from the scenario seed and is never drawn per run: the mapping is a property of the corpus, not of a run, because the extract is a single replayed hour and the same airframes recur in every run of a batch. One aircraft therefore carries one pseudonym across every run, and scn-001's byte-identical guarantee for a given type, parameters and seed is unaffected, since nothing about the mapping varies with those three values. The seed itself is NOT committed and is NOT written into the manifest. Amended 2026-08-21: the item previously required the seed to be recorded in the corpus manifest, which is committed. That is a defect rather than a detail. icao24 is a 24-bit space of roughly 16.7 million values, so a reader holding the seed and the derivation function reconstructs the entire mapping by exhaustive search in seconds -- a published seed is a readable reverse mapping, which this item forbids in the same sentence. The seed is therefore read from the environment, its key documented in backend/.env.example alongside the existing convention that secrets are never committed (NFR-401), and what the manifest records is the SHA-256 fingerprint of the seed rather than the seed. That preserves what recording it was for -- a seed change remains a detectable, recorded corpus-level event sitting beside the extract checksum, rather than a silent one -- without publishing the value. The consequence is a limitation to be stated rather than hidden: the mapping is machine-local, so a reader who rebuilds the corpus obtains different pseudonyms from the author's. Every reported metric still reproduces exactly, because nothing downstream reads a pseudonym's value -- it is an opaque grouping key, and detection, evidence bundling and scoring are invariant under relabelling. What does not reproduce is a specific label quoted in a thesis figure, which is the correct trade: a figure whose labels a reader could reverse is the disclosure the item exists to prevent. Failure case: a real icao24 or callsign appearing in an API response, an evidence bundle, a hypothesis, a hosted-provider request payload, or a rendered screen fails the spec, because OpenSky Data License Agreement section 3(i) requires aircraft identifiers to be de-identified for any publication or other disclosure and section 3(iii) forbids making the data available outside the licensee's institute. A second failure case: the same aircraft carrying different pseudonyms in two runs against the same corpus, which breaks track continuity across a replay and makes a batch non-comparable; deriving the pseudonym from the scenario seed produces exactly this and fails the spec. A third failure case: retaining the source identifier in the observation payload beside the pseudonym, which satisfies the letter of the mapping while leaving the real value one query away. A fourth failure case: committing the seed, or writing it into the manifest, which makes every pseudonym reversible by exhaustive search over the icao24 space and reduces the whole item to theatre. A fifth failure case: truncating the digest far enough that two of the corpus's 1,445 distinct icao24 values collide onto one pseudonym, which merges two airframes into one track and corrupts every continuity rule downstream without raising anything. Refs: FR-111, NFR-405, NFR-401, FR-101, FR-104, US-E2, AC-02, dal-001, dal-002, dal-003, adp-001, adp-003, adp-004, evb-001, ai-004, docs/qa.md section 22, docs/qa.md section 26.

OpenSky replay adapter, a pure windowed reader over the archived extract. Input: the bounding-box-filtered OpenSky extract at data/opensky/opensky_extract.parquet, its committed manifest, and a bounded half-open window of source time. Output: source records in the DAL's source-record shape -- source_id, source_type, observation_type, timestamp, location, and a track payload carrying icao24, callsign, altitude_m, velocity_ms, heading_deg, vertical_rate_ms, on_ground, position_staleness_s and contact_staleness_s -- yielded in ascending time order and handed to ingest_batch, which converts them into canonical track observations. Amended 2026-08-23, three changes. First, the adapter holds no clock. The item previously took 'a replay position in simulated time', which put a replay cursor inside the adapter. It is now a pure windowed reader: given a half-open window over source time it yields the records falling in it and keeps no position between calls. The simulated clock belongs to the scenario runner, scn-001, because detection latency is measured in simulated scenario time from event onset to anomaly emission, and two components each holding a notion of now makes that measurement ambiguous at exactly the point it has to be defensible; it also keeps the adapter testable offline against a small fixture with no scenario machinery in scope. Second, the extract is not committed. The item previously described 'a committed Parquet file' and replay 'reproducible from a fresh clone with no download step'. Both were true when written and were falsified by adp-004's licence reversal: OpenSky Data License Agreement section 3(iii) forbids making the data available outside the licensee's institute, so opensky_extract.parquet is gitignored. Reproducibility from a fresh clone now runs through adp-006 -- python -m app.corpus.build with explicit licence acceptance -- which re-downloads roughly 180 MB against the manifest's recorded checksum and re-filters. The adapter's own guarantee is unchanged and is the one that matters here: it reads from file only and never opens a socket. Third, a Parquet reader has to be written. read_rows in app/corpus/extract.py reads the raw tarball's gzipped CSV, not the extract, and write_parquet has no counterpart; the previous handoff recorded read_rows as already yielding the rows this item replays, which was wrong. The reader takes its types from the schema embedded in the artefact rather than inferring them or importing the writer's column list; verified against the real extract, ParquetFile.schema_arrow returns the writer's fields in the writer's order, so the file is asked rather than a shared constant. A reader that inferred types would silently disagree with the writer as soon as a column is entirely null within a window, and one that imported parquet_schema would restate what the artefact already carries and drift from it the moment the two disagreed. Scope, settled 2026-08-25: the item delivers app/adapters/opensky.py, a module that imports nothing from app.corpus -- the arrow must not point from the consumer of the artefact back to the build-time tool that downloads and filters it. Three functions. read_window is the pure reader: path and half-open window in, source records out, no DAL involvement and no state between calls. replay_window is thin wiring that drives read_window into ingest_batch and returns the IngestResult, taking the ingest context, the repository and the pseudonymiser as injected arguments and importing no concrete implementation of either.
