The ladder end to end over all 240 runs, which anom-013 shipped without: 60 of 60 rf-sensor-fault decided as possible_sensor_fault, 60 of 60 gnss-degradation as possible_interference_zone, 20 of 20 ambiguous-mixed-evidence as a sensor fault by the design recorded on anom-007, 75 of 80 aircraft-coverage-gap correctly silent and 19 of 20 normal-baseline correctly silent. The 6 of 100 false reports on runs staging nothing on the RF grid are anom-001's own false positive rate promoted one layer, already recorded on anom-007 and owned by anom-014. Five gnss-degradation runs and one rf-sensor-fault run carry a second anomaly of the other type in a different zone; that is not a precedence violation, because anom-013 guarantees at most one answer per zone and never per run, and a run may genuinely hold a broken receiver in one place and interference in another. Re-measured 2026-09-18 on the regenerated corpus, and the gating decision is unchanged while both sides of its argument moved. What reaches step three is now 60 of 60 gnss-degradation and 0 of every other arm -- the single rf-sensor-fault leak is gone, because anom-014 removed the spurious episode that produced it, so nothing false arrives here at all and a gate still has nothing to catch. The cost of gating fell sharply: the excess now clears the threshold on 58 of 60 rather than 26 of 40, with a median of 9.61 against 3.87, and there are no unusable windows where there were seven. So a gate would now lose 2 runs rather than 14. The decision stands on the same reasoning it was made on -- an unmeasurable benefit against a measured cost -- and it is worth recording that the cost falling by a factor of seven does not change a benefit that is still zero. Corroboration also improved and remains the honest limitation: 18 of 60 zones corroborated against 7 of 61, 1 not corroborated against 7, and 41 of 60 still NOT MEASURABLE against 47 of 61. Two thirds of reported zones continue to have no measurable track side, so any claim about fusion must still be stated as the radio evidence with an occasional corroborating note.

Data-source issue rule, rule ID SOURCE-GAP. Input: track dropout clusters and the set of RF anomalies for the same window and area. Output: an anomaly of type possible_data_source_issue when dropouts are present and no co-located RF anomaly exists. Constraints: this rule is the discriminator that keeps a coverage gap from being reported as interference; it is mutually exclusive with anom-005 for the same cluster. Failure case: an aircraft-coverage-gap scenario producing possible_interference_zone instead of possible_data_source_issue fails the spec. Refs: FR-306, scn-002, anom-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.3. Amended 2026-09-17, after measuring what this rule would have to detect, and the amendment records that it is NOT built and why. Six findings, in the order they were taken. First, the defensive half of this item's job is already done, by anom-013 rather than by anything here. The item's stated purpose is to be the discriminator that keeps a coverage gap from being reported as interference. Measured over 240 runs, 0 of 40 aircraft-coverage-gap runs reach anom-005 at all, because that type stages nothing on the RF grid and anom-005's trigger is an RF anomaly. The misattribution this rule exists to prevent can no longer occur, and it is prevented by the absence of a strong signal rather than by the presence of a weak one. What remains for this item is the positive claim: saying we are not hearing aircraft here when that is true. Second, that positive claim cannot be made on the current corpus, and the reason is the open question already recorded on scn-006 rather than anything about this rule. Since that fix a coverage-gap run stages a mean of 1.7 aircraft and 11 of 40 stage none at all, so a quarter of the arm has an empty answer key and is by construction indistinguishable from its control. Third, the effect that remains is real and unmistakable and far too small to act on. Over 40 seed-matched pairs against rf-sensor-fault controls -- same seed, same corpus window, same aircraft, nothing staged on tracks in 40 of 40 -- a coverage-gap run holds a mean of 16.1 track-gap findings against its control's 15.1, and never fewer: 23 pairs strictly greater, 17 tied, 0 lower. Zero discordant losses in 40 pairs is overwhelming evidence that the effect exists. It is also one finding in fifteen, and a detector sees one run without its control, so it cannot tell 16 from 15. Fourth, the zone-level design does not rescue it; it makes matters worse. Proposing zones by clustering the findings (anom-004) and scoring each by anom-012's rate excess, then taking the strongest zone per run, gives staged against control of 7 to 3 at a 20 km cluster radius, 5 to 4 at 40 km and 4 to 2 at 60 km, with the remainder tied. That is chance. The machinery destroys a signal that raw counting preserves, and the mechanism is visible in anom-005's measurement: a ratio taken over a disc holding one to three findings is dominated by anom-012's smoothing term, so taking the maximum across zones selects for small-sample noise rather than for effect. Fifth, building it as specified would be actively wrong rather than merely weak. The rule as written fires when dropouts are present and no co-located RF anomaly exists; a quiet run genuinely holds about 15 findings and no RF anomaly, so the rule would fire on every normal-baseline run in the corpus and destroy anom-008's zero-anomalies control. A discrimination threshold is therefore mandatory, and the measurements above say no threshold on the available quantities separates the arm from its control. Sixth, what unblocks it is a generator change and not a detector one, which is scn-007. This item stays specified and unbuilt until a corpus exists in which a coverage gap is a zone-level event, and the measurement above is then repeated before any threshold here is chosen. Recorded as a threat to validity in the meantime: the detection layer currently has no rule for the aircraft-coverage-gap arm, so that arm contributes only correct non-detections to eval-002 and must not be reported as though the system had been tested on it. Refs adds: anom-012, anom-013, scn-006, scn-007, eval-002. Re-opened 2026-09-18 on the regenerated corpus, and the reason is measurement rather than optimism. The item was closed as unbuildable on two findings: a run-level excess of one finding in fifteen, and zone-level scoring at chance (7:3, 5:4, 4:2 at 20/40/60 km cluster radii). With scn-007 putting a floor of five staged aircraft under every run, both were re-measured over 60 seed-matched pairs. The run-level picture is better and still not usable: 16.9 findings against the control's 14.2, 57 of 60 pairs won with 3 ties and 0 losses, and detected staged dropouts up from 1.07 to 3.05 per run -- but the excess of 2.7 sits against a control spread of 3.3, so it is 0.8 of a standard deviation and a detector seeing one run without its control still cannot tell 17 from 14. That was predicted on this item before the regeneration and the prediction held. The zone-level picture is the one that changed: 20 wins to 7 losses at 20 km, 14 to 8 at 40 km, 10 to 5 at 60 km, where every radius was previously indistinguishable from a coin. At 20 km, 20 against 7 discordant pairs is about one in fifty by sign test. That is a real signal in the machinery this rule would actually use, and it exists because five staged aircraft put enough co-located dropouts in one place for a cluster to form where 1.7 could not. The item is therefore buildable to try, NOT known to be buildable: a sign test on discordant pairs says the staged zone tends to beat its control, and says nothing about whether a threshold exists that separates them on a single run, which is the question a detector faces and which needs its own measurement before any threshold is chosen. Build it against that measurement, not against these figures. Refs: scn-007, anom-004, anom-012, anom-008, eval-002. Closed again 2026-09-18, on the threshold measurement this item asked for, and the item is now closed on a stronger basis than the first closure. The re-opening rested on a sign test over matched pairs (20 wins to 7 at a 20 km cluster radius) and recorded that it said nothing about whether a fixed threshold separates a staged zone from an unstaged one on a single run. That measurement has been taken, pre-registered in measurements/corpus/source_gap_threshold_prereg.md with its populations, its operating-point rule and its failure bar fixed in advance, and scored on a held-out base seed the threshold was not chosen on. Five findings. First, the answer is no: the best development operating point leaving anom-008's quiet arm silent is a 60 km cluster radius, a minimum zone size of four findings and an excess threshold of 11.53, giving 7 of 40 coverage gaps caught, and the held-out seed gives 3 of 20 with zero quiet-arm alarms. 0.15 against a pre-registered bar of 0.25. Second, and this is the finding that closes the item rather than merely failing it, the rule points the wrong way: at that operating point it fires on 6 of 20 gnss-degradation runs against 3 of 20 coverage gaps, twice as often on the arm it is not for as on the arm it is. anom-013 orders SENSOR-FAULT, SOURCE-GAP, FUSION-SPATIAL, so SOURCE-GAP outranks the interference rule and a firing there can take the zone before FUSION-SPATIAL is offered it. Building this rule would put the one arm the ladder gets right 60 of 60 at risk to catch a seventh of an arm it currently ignores. Whether those zones actually overlap is not measured, so the hazard is established and its size is not. Third, the ceiling is low everywhere and not merely at the zero-false-alarm constraint: the best Youden's J anywhere on the development sweep is 0.275, at a 0.38 quiet-arm rate anom-008 forbids outright, and anom-012 reported 0.23 to 0.40 on a curve this project already calls weak. Fourth, the mechanism is visible and is the one predicted when the item was first closed. The statistic saturates: at a size floor of one every arm reaches the same maximum ratio of 198.78 and the medians differ by 0.6, because taking the maximum across zones selects the noisiest small sample and every run has one. Separation appears only at a size floor of four or more, by which point the qualifying population has fallen to about two thirds of runs. Fifth, a population correction that outlives this item: ambiguous-mixed-evidence shares aircraft-coverage-gap's SUPPRESS mode and rf-sensor-fault perturbs tracks not at all, so at a shared seed the first pair and the second pair produce identical track findings, verified exactly. Any track-side figure quoting 120 negatives or treating the ambiguous arm as independent evidence is counting 60 seeds twice. The out-of-sample agreement was good, 0.17 development against 0.15 holdout, so this is a reliable measurement of a weak effect rather than a noisy one, and repeating it on more runs of the same corpus will not change it. What would change it is a generator change, as the first closure also concluded: a coverage gap must become a zone-level event distinguishable from a frozen one. The threat to validity recorded against eval-002 therefore stands unchanged and is now the settled position rather than a pending question: the detection layer has no rule for the aircraft-coverage-gap arm, its 60 of 60 correct non-detections are correct only because nothing judges that arm, and it must not be reported as though the system had been tested on it. Options not taken, recorded 2026-09-18 so the closure states what was declined and why rather than only what failed. Five were available and none is impossible. First, build it at a more sensitive operating point and accept the false alarms: declined because it breaks anom-008, a passing item, and because the arm it would falsely fire on is the one the ladder currently decides correctly 60 of 60, so a rule with an adverse likelihood ratio is worse than no rule. Second, build it as this item originally specified, firing on dropouts wherever no co-located RF anomaly exists: declined on the first closure's own measurement, since a quiet run genuinely holds about 15 discontinuities and no RF anomaly, so the rule fires on every baseline run. The RF side is a veto and not a discriminator. Third, change the statistic, summing or counting qualifying zones rather than taking the maximum: both ends of that family have now been measured and both fail, the run-level aggregate at 0.8 standard deviations and the zone-level maximum here, but intermediate forms were not tried and this is the cheapest untried option. Fourth, raise the staged fraction so a gap removes most aircraft in an area: possible with a mean eligible pool of 23.4, and declined because it changes what the scenario means -- removing most aircraft over a region is an outage rather than a coverage gap, and an easier problem than the one scoped -- and because it needs a third corpus generation that would invalidate every detection figure measured on v2. Fifth, change the generator so a coverage gap is a zone-level event by construction, suppressing a contiguous area rather than a selected set of aircraft: this is the option both closures identify as the one that would actually work, and it is declined on cost rather than on merit, needing a third regeneration, a re-measurement of the whole detection chapter and a re-derivation of scn-007's floor. Recorded as future work. Consequence for the corpus, and it is not confined to this item: with this rule absent, ambiguous-mixed-evidence and rf-sensor-fault are indistinguishable in the detection layer's reportable output, both decided possible_sensor_fault on all 60 runs. tracks.py gives the ambiguous arm the same SUPPRESS mode as the coverage-gap arm, so their track findings are identical at a shared seed, and fusion.py consumes only anom-007's environmental verdict, so on a single-receiver run that track evidence never reaches a claim. The arm built to present anom-013 with conflicting evidence therefore cannot produce a second bid. See anom-013 and eval-002, both amended with this.

Sensor fault rule, rule ID SENSOR-FAULT. Input: an RF sensor reporting abnormal readings, the readings of its spatial neighbours in the same window, and the readings of the frequency-adjacent channels on the sensor itself. Output: an anomaly of type possible_sensor_fault when the sensor is abnormal and its spatial neighbours are nominal, with the frequency-adjacency test recorded as a distinct piece of evidence rather than folded into the spatial one. Constraints: spatial neighbour selection is a spatial query with a configured radius, not a hard-coded sensor list; frequency neighbour selection is the adjacent channel indices on the same sensor. A real emission raises adjacent channels together, so an isolated single-channel deviation with clean neighbours is evidence about the sensor rather than the environment. Failure case: several adjacent sensors all reporting abnormal readings must not raise a sensor-fault anomaly, since that pattern indicates an environmental cause. A second failure case: a deviation spanning all eight channels on one sensor being reported with the same confidence as a single-channel one, since the broadband pattern is weaker evidence of a fault. Refs: FR-307, FR-108, scn-002, scn-005, db-004, anom-001, anom-002. Amended 2026-09-17, before implementation, after reading the layout and the threshold rule this consumes. Eight decisions. First, the input is anom-001's whole result and not only its anomalies. That rule reports the cells it could not judge alongside the ones it could, and this is the first consumer that would otherwise read that silence as cleanliness: a neighbour reporting nothing because it had no usable baseline is not a neighbour reporting nominal. The verdict is therefore three-valued rather than two -- a neighbour with an overlapping anomaly settles it as environmental, neighbours all judged and all clean settles it as a fault, and neighbours clean with any cell unjudged is recorded as undecided with the reason rather than as a fault. Positive evidence of an environmental cause outranks missing data, and missing data outranks inferring that nothing seen means nothing happened. Second, neighbour selection is by great-circle distance from the layout at a configured radius, defaulting to the layout's own discrimination radius, which scn-005 already validates as leaving every sensor at least one neighbour inside it and at least one beyond. A sensor with no neighbour inside the configured radius compares against nothing, and the vacuous case -- no neighbours, therefore no abnormal neighbours, therefore a fault -- would turn every RF anomaly in the layout into a sensor fault. That case is refused and recorded as undecided, which is this item's third failure case. Third, the unit of judgement is one sensor over one merged window and not one cell episode. A fault is a property of a receiver; per-episode output would report one broken box once per affected channel and leave any count of sensor faults reading as eight. Fourth, confidence is Low, Medium or High (ui-001) and it qualifies the attribution rather than the deviation. The size of the deviation is already carried by anom-001 as a severity, and the two are different quantities: how far past normal a reading went, against how strongly the pattern implicates the instrument. High is a single channel with both frequency neighbours clean; Medium is a deviation across some but not all of the plan; Low is every channel on the sensor, which is this item's second failure case -- a broadband elevation on one receiver is also what a wideband emitter parked beside it would produce. Fifth, the frequency-adjacency test is carried as its own field with its own list of the channels checked, not folded into the spatial verdict, because the two are evidence of different kinds and an analyst reading the bundle needs to see which one carries the argument. Sixth, episode overlap is inclusive at both endpoints. An anom-001 episode's end is its last exceeding reading rather than the first quiet one, so a neighbour whose episode ends on the tick this one starts genuinely overlapped it by one reading, and a strict comparison would call that neighbour clean. Seventh, this rule consults no track evidence, enforced by what it can be handed rather than by remembering not to: its input carries RF findings and a layout and has nowhere to put a track finding. anom-013 places it first for that reason, and the enforcement is what makes the ordering a property of the types rather than of the caller. Eighth, one thing this item cannot measure, stated rather than left silent: all 240 stored runs are narrowband, so the Low band exists in unit tests and has no corpus behind it. A broadband arm is a separate generation item, and the confidence ordering must not be quoted as measured until it exists. The measurement this item owes, and the reason it is built before anom-012's radius is fixed: anom-013's ordering assumes this rule claims the runs whose truth is a sensor fault, and that assumption is untested. To be recorded here once measured -- the catch rate over the 60 rf-sensor-fault runs, the false-fire rate over the 60 gnss-degradation and 20 normal-baseline runs, and separately the rate over the 20 ambiguous-mixed-evidence runs, which stage a single sensor by construction and which this rule is therefore expected to claim. That last is a property of the scenario design rather than a defect in the rule, and it is reported rather than excluded. Refs adds: anom-013, anom-008, anom-012, ui-001, docs/phase8_detection.md. Corrected 2026-09-17, by the measurement this item owed, and the correction is a reversal of the first decision of the amendment above. Measured over 240 stored runs with the baseline built from the 20 quiet ones: the rule claims 60 of 60 rf-sensor-fault runs, on the staged receiver and inside the staged window, which is the assumption anom-013 rests on and it holds without qualification. It also claimed 21 of 60 gnss-degradation runs on a staged receiver inside the staged window, which is a misattribution of the same class as the one anom-013 was written to remove, in the opposite direction. The cause is not the neighbour radius and not the layout. The injected elevation is 8 dB scaled per cell per tick by 1 + 0.25 of a standard normal draw, and anom-001's threshold is 6 dB, so about one tick in six falls short and ends the episode: a staged cell emits a median of six episodes where the incident is one. Two receivers loud through the same 300 s can therefore have fragments that never overlap, and each reads as isolated from the other. The defect is in reading the neighbour's nominality off another rule's episodes rather than off its readings, which is what the item asked for in its original wording -- the readings of its spatial neighbours in the same window -- and what the amendment above replaced with anom-001's findings. The original wording was right. The input is therefore the run's RF observations and the anom-002 baseline table alongside anom-001's findings: the findings say which of the subject's cells are abnormal and which cells nobody could judge, and the readings say whether a neighbour was nominal. Measured, over the 120 staged runs: a neighbour the incident also touched sits 2.51 dB above its own baseline at the 5th percentile and 4.46 dB at the median during a window this rule was about to call a fault, while a neighbour the incident did not touch sits at -0.05 dB at the median and 1.58 dB at the 95th. The populations separate, and a bar of 2 dB in the gap between them removes all 21 misattributions while leaving all 60 catches intact. The neighbouring bars are reported with it rather than only the chosen one: 1.0 and 1.5 dB also give 0 of 60, 3.0 dB gives 5 and 4.0 dB gives 7, so the choice sits on a plateau and not on a cliff, and the bar is a policy field with a measured default rather than a literal. The rejected alternative is recorded because it also works on this corpus and is cheaper: treating a neighbour episode within 30 s of the window as overlapping it gives 0 of 60 and 60 of 60 as well. It is rejected because it answers a different question -- whether the neighbour was anomalous recently, rather than whether it was nominal now -- and because it only works while the neighbour crosses anom-001's threshold somewhere nearby. The 8 dB elevation is the generator's choice, not a property of interference; a weaker emitter, or a neighbour further out, raises a neighbour by 3 or 4 dB and produces no episode at any tolerance, and the tolerance form would then read it as nominal for ever. The readings form sees it directly. Measured in support: of the 37 staged-neighbour measurements above, none exceeded anom-001's 6 dB threshold during the window in question, so every one of them was invisible to a test built on episodes. Consequences recorded rather than deferred. Nominality is judged in the direction the metric chooses -- power upwards, SNR downwards -- derived from the baseline table's own metric rather than configured, because a direction a caller can set wrongly is a silent wrong answer. A neighbour with no baseline or no readings in the window cannot be measured and is undecided, which is the same three-valued verdict as before with a more direct reason. A track observation handed in among the RF ones is refused rather than skipped, on anom-001's argument, which is also what keeps the no-track-evidence guarantee structural now that the rule takes observations at all. Two further results from the same measurement, neither of them about the neighbour test. First, anom-001 raises at least one anomaly on 13 of 80 aircraft-coverage-gap runs and 1 of 20 normal-baseline runs, all of which stage nothing on the RF grid, and this rule promotes every one of them to a sensor fault at High confidence. Those 14 fires are all single-channel episodes of 20 s or less, which is anom-001's false-positive rate surfacing one layer up rather than a defect here; the rule has no minimum duration and a one-tick blip is not evidence about an instrument. A minimum-duration constraint belongs to anom-001 and is left to a separate item rather than patched here. Second, the rule claims 20 of 20 ambiguous-mixed-evidence runs, at High confidence, with no trace of ambiguity in the output -- which follows from that type staging a single receiver by construction and from anom-013 offering a claimed zone to no later rule. That is a property of the scenario design meeting the ordering, it is reported rather than excluded, and it is a threat to the validity of any evaluation that treats the ambiguous type as a test of whether the system can express uncertainty. Re-measured 2026-09-17 on the rebuilt rule, same 240 runs, same baseline and same anom-001 policy, the only change being that nominality is read from the neighbours' readings. The rule claims 60 of 60 rf-sensor-fault runs on the staged receiver inside the staged window, and 0 of 60 gnss-degradation runs, against 21 of 60 before. The window it reports now recovers the incident rather than a fragment of it: a median of 300 s against a staged duration of 300 s, where the episode-based version gave a median of 20 s, and the number of faults raised per sensor-fault run falls from about five to 1.13. The extension overruns slightly at the top -- 390 s at the maximum -- because a tick either side of the incident can still read above the 2 dB bar on ordinary noise, which is the cost of a bar set low enough to keep the window contiguous and is recorded rather than trimmed. Two residual behaviours, both reported rather than suppressed. Runs that stage nothing on the RF grid still raise a fault on 6 of 100 of them (5 of 80 aircraft-coverage-gap and 1 of 20 normal-baseline), down from 14 of 100: these are anom-001 false positives promoted one layer up, and the residue survives because a short episode can still sustain a 2 dB mean across its own window. A minimum-duration constraint belongs to anom-001 and is left to a separate item. And the rule still claims 20 of 20 ambiguous-mixed-evidence runs at High confidence, for the reason recorded above: that type stages a single receiver by construction. The new refusal this rebuild added, which is what removed most of the false positives: an episode whose window the readings do not sustain -- the receiver sitting inside the bar of its own baseline across the whole window anom-001's episode seeds -- is undecided rather than a fault, because a threshold crossing that the window does not bear out is not evidence about an instrument. It accounts for the undecided dismissals in the measurement: 8 on coverage-gap runs, 3 on gnss-degradation, 3 on rf-sensor-fault, 1 on ambiguous.

Correct non-detection on a normal-baseline run. Input: a completed normal-baseline scenario run with no injected deviation. Output: zero anomalies of any type. Constraints: this is a required positive behaviour of the detection engine, not an absence of behaviour; it is asserted for every detector, not only in aggregate. Failure case: any anomaly raised on a clean run fails the spec, because the false-positive rate reported in eval-002 becomes meaningless if the engine is noisy on clean data. Refs: FR-308, US-R5, AC-04, scn-002, eval-002, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 14. Amended 2026-09-14, before any detector was written against it, on measuring the corpus. The constraint that a normal-baseline run produces zero anomalies of any type is scoped here to the reportable ones -- the fused rules an analyst is actually shown, being anom-005's possible_interference_zone, anom-006's possible_data_source_issue and anom-007's possible_sensor_fault. It does not count the intermediate findings those rules consume. The measurement that forces this: a quiet run contains roughly 138 aircraft, of about 530 seen, whose reported position staleness exceeds 100 s, and about 8 intervals between consecutive reports exceeding 100 s before filtering. Those are real properties of real replayed data, not defects in the detector and not artefacts of the pipeline, and a rule requiring the track detector to emit zero of them would be requiring it to be wrong. Read the other way, the unamended constraint would be satisfiable only by a detector that failed to notice genuine discontinuities in its input. The control's purpose is unchanged and is what the scoping protects: on a run with nothing staged, nothing reaches the analyst, and the false-positive rate in eval-002 is computed from that. Two obligations are added rather than dropped. The rate of intermediate findings on quiet runs is recorded alongside the reportable count, because it is the number that would move if the corpus or the generator changed underneath the detectors and nothing else would show it. And the assertion stays per detector rather than in aggregate, as this item already requires -- for an intermediate producer the assertion is that its findings are within the recorded background rather than that there are none. Failure cases amended. A reportable anomaly of any of the three fused types raised on a clean run still fails the spec, unchanged. A detector reporting zero intermediate findings on a quiet run now also fails it, because the corpus is known to contain them and silence means the detector did not look. Recorded as a threat to validity: this scoping makes the false-positive rate a statement about the fused layer only, and a reader could mistake it for a statement about detection as a whole. The evaluation reports both numbers for that reason. Refs adds: anom-010, anom-005, anom-006, anom-007, dal-001.

Detection latency measurement. Input: an anomaly and its scenario run ground truth. Output: latency as the simulated-time delta between injected event onset and anomaly emission. Constraints: simulated scenario time only, never wall clock; the definition is fixed before any measurement code exists, per the Track 0 item in docs/implementation.md; the unit is recorded alongside the value. Failure case: a latency that changes when the same run is replayed on faster hardware fails the spec, because it proves wall-clock time leaked in. Refs: FR-309, FR-1002, NFR-601, scn-001, eval-002.

Track continuity rule, rule ID TRACK-GAP. Input: aircraft position observations for one scenario run, a staleness threshold, and the run's simulated time window. Output: a track_continuity_gap anomaly per affected aircraft, carrying the gap's onset and end in simulated time, its duration, the last known position as the anomaly's location, and the observation IDs either side of the gap. Constraints: staleness is the simulated-time interval between consecutive reports for one pseudonymised aircraft, never wall clock, consistent with anom-009; the threshold is configuration, not a literal in the rule; the rule is deterministic, so the same observations always give the same anomalies. Failure cases: an aircraft whose last report is the final one before the run window closes must raise nothing, since every track still in flight is stale at the end of every window and a rule that fires there fires on all of them at once; an aircraft that leaves the bounding box or lands must raise nothing, because ceasing to report is correct behaviour in both cases and neither is a discontinuity; and a gap one interval below threshold must raise nothing while one interval above raises exactly one. Refs: FR-304, FR-301, FR-306, adp-001, adp-004, anom-002, anom-004, anom-006, anom-008, db-004, scn-002, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.3. Written 2026-09-14, on picking up Phase 8, because FR-304 had no spec item at all. Nine anom items covered eight of the nine detection requirements; anom-004 clusters track-continuity anomalies and anom-006 consumes track dropout clusters, and nothing in the backlog produced one. The rule the fusion pair is built on was the one rule nobody had written down. Two decisions. First, the unit is the gap rather than the aircraft: one anomaly per discontinuity, not one per stale track, because anom-004 clusters discontinuities by location and an aircraft with two gaps in different places is two pieces of spatial evidence rather than one. Second, and the reason this item cannot be written as a bare threshold: the corpus contains genuine dropouts, and normal-baseline replays the corpus. The coverage acceptance check of 2026-08-19 measured 10 of 948 tracks (1.05 per cent) carrying a genuine interior airborne dropout, with seven of the ten falling in the 100-300 s band that scenario type 4 injects into. A staleness rule over a normal-baseline run will therefore fire on real corpus gaps, and anom-008 requires that run to raise zero anomalies of any type. The conflict is settled here rather than discovered as a failing anom-008 test. Raising the threshold above 300 s is rejected: it would blind the detector to exactly the band the injected gaps occupy, buying a clean false-positive rate by disabling the measurement it is the control for. Relaxing anom-008 to anomalies attributable to injection is rejected: FR-308 makes correct non-detection a required behaviour, and a control that permits known firings is not a control. The accepted answer is the exclusion already owed by the Track 0 residue -- the generator refuses the ten identified tracks as corpus-window content, using the coverage report to identify them -- extended from injection sites, where it was owed, to baseline windows, where it is equally needed and was not previously noticed. Added failure case: a normal-baseline run raising a track_continuity_gap from a genuine corpus dropout fails this item as well as anom-008, because it means the exclusion was not applied. Recorded limitation: the exclusion removes real data to make a false-positive rate measurable, so the reported rate is conditional on it, and the measured rate with and without the exclusion is owed to the evaluation. Amended 2026-09-14, before tests, after measuring the corpus rather than reasoning about it. The corpus-dropout decision written into this item that morning was wrong by about two orders of magnitude and is corrected here rather than quietly replaced. It assumed the ten tracks adp-008 names were the whole false-positive problem. Measured across the twenty normal-baseline runs in the development database, the background is this: of roughly 530 aircraft seen per run, 137.7 reach a peak reported position staleness above 100 s, 19.3 above 300 s, and 1.0 above 600 s. The equivalent gnss-degradation figures are 141.1, 20.7 and 0.6 -- so the staged signature is about 3.4 aircraft per run against a background of 137.7, and above 600 s the quiet runs are higher than the staged ones. No threshold separates them at any value. The cause is not a tuning error: the injection stages disruptions of 100-300 s because that is what a plausible real coverage failure looks like, and it is also what a real one is, so the staged effect was designed into the densest part of the distribution it has to be told apart from. Five decisions follow. First, this item's output is an intermediate finding and not a reportable anomaly. It is computed for anom-004 to cluster and is never shown to an analyst, for the reason anom-008 is amended alongside: a quiet run genuinely contains of the order of 138 track discontinuities that are real properties of real data, so a control requiring zero of them would require the detector to be wrong. What the rule detects is staleness; what it cannot do is attribute it, and attribution is spatial and cross-modal by design -- the background gaps are scattered across 309,000 square kilometres while a staged one sits inside a zone about 20 km across with a raised noise floor over it. Second, there are two detection mechanisms because the two scenario types stage differently, and a rule with only one of them is blind to one type. gnss-degradation rewrites the reported position staleness and the rows keep arriving; aircraft-coverage-gap suppresses the rows entirely, so nothing arrives to read a field from. The rule therefore reports a frozen_position finding from a reading whose position staleness exceeds the threshold, and a not_heard finding from an interval between consecutive reports of one aircraft that exceeds it. The shape is carried on the finding, because it is exactly what anom-005 and anom-006 need to tell interference from a data-source failure. Third, the frozen_position mechanism additionally requires contact to be fresh, and this is a measured decision rather than a tidy one. Requiring fresh contact alongside stale position -- the two-clock discriminator dal-001 documents -- narrows the quiet-run background from 137.7 aircraft per run to 24.6 while leaving the staged margin unchanged at 3.4, so the signal-to-background ratio improves from about one in forty to about one in seven. It is the single largest improvement available to this rule and it costs nothing. Fourth, two filters apply, and they are the same two the bounding-box sweep and adp-008 both needed. An aircraft on the ground is excluded from both mechanisms, because a parked aircraft stops reporting for the uninteresting reason that it has been switched off. A not_heard finding additionally requires both ends of the gap to lie inside the corpus bounding box by a margin, because an aircraft that flies out of the box and back leaves an interval with nothing in it and nothing went wrong; the interior test does not apply to frozen_position, which has no gap to bracket. Measured on the quiet runs: 164 intervals exceed 100 s, 32 survive the airborne filter, 23 survive both, and those 23 belong to four aircraft every one of which is on the adp-008 list, with none unlisted. Omitting the two filters would mean four-fifths of the findings were artefacts of having drawn a box and of aircraft being switched off. Fifth, the exclusion list stays the generator's responsibility and is not duplicated here. The measurement above is an independent validation of adp-008 from a different code path -- built at corpus-build time from raw archive rows, checked here against pseudonymised observations in PostGIS after a full replay -- and it also confirms the list is not being applied to baseline windows, which is owed work on the generator rather than a defence to add to the detector. Failure cases added. A reading whose position is stale but whose contact is equally stale must not raise a frozen_position finding, because that shape is an aircraft not being heard from rather than one reporting a frozen position. A gap whose either end lies outside the bounding-box margin must raise no not_heard finding. A gap either of whose ends has the aircraft on the ground must raise nothing. The superseded failure case about a normal-baseline run raising a track_continuity_gap no longer applies and is withdrawn: a quiet run raises many, by design, and anom-008 is amended to say what the control actually counts. Refs adds: adp-008, dal-001, anom-005, anom-006. Amended 2026-09-19, on the evb-002 traceability measurement, and the amendment is about what a finding cites rather than what it detects. A finding carries two kinds of time and this item had conflated them: the window is the rule's conclusion, and the reports it read are its evidence. For a not_heard gap the two coincide, because the window ends ARE the reports either side of the silence. For a frozen_position gap they cannot coincide: started_at is the first stale report's timestamp minus the staleness that report declares, a reconstruction of when the position went stale, and that instant is by definition the one moment in the whole window at which nothing was recorded -- the position had stopped updating, which is what the finding is about. Measured over 24 real bundles from 40 runs: of 1,021 cited coordinates 91 resolve to zero rows, every one of them a frozen_position start, with every RF coordinate and every not_heard coordinate resolving cleanly; a focused check over three runs put it at 48 of 48 frozen starts unresolvable and 3 of 3 not_heard findings clean at both ends. The finding therefore gains observed_at, the timestamps of the first and last report the rule actually read, which equal the window for not_heard and do not for frozen_position. started_at is unchanged and deliberately so: when the position went stale remains the right answer to the question the window asks, and moving it to the first stale report's own timestamp would make every frozen finding shorter than the event it describes, which would quietly change anom-012's during-window counts. Note what nearly hid this -- a test written over a coverage-gap finding passes, because both of its ends are real rows, so the fixture would have proved traceability working on the only shape that cannot break it. Same class as the baseline test that had to be rebuilt because it could not fail. Failure case added: a frozen_position finding whose observed_at start equals its started_at fails the spec, because that is the reconstruction being written back into the citation. Refs adds: evb-002, db-008.

Track-gap detection sensitivity, and the recall figure the fusion rules depend on. Input: the stored scenario runs with their ground truth, and the TRACK-GAP rule from anom-010. Output: a per-aircraft recall figure for each staged scenario type, measured against the answer key rather than against a control, together with an account of where the undetected staged aircraft are lost -- the perturber's choice of which records to touch, the rule's airborne filter, its interior-to-box filter, or the requirement for a bracketing report either side of an absence. Constraints: measured on at least two independently seeded batches before any figure is reported as a property of the detector, because the figures here come from one; the answer key is the ground truth recorded at generation time by scn-002, never derived from the detector's own output; the investigation changes no detector behaviour by itself, so any fix it motivates is a separate item with its own tests. Failure cases: a recall figure quoted without the batch and policy it was measured under fails the spec, per the project's rule that a measurement without its conditions is a memory; and an account that attributes the loss without measuring it -- naming a filter as the cause rather than counting what each filter removes -- fails it too. Written 2026-09-15, on measuring anom-004 before writing it. The measurement that forces this item: across the seed-matched runs, 119 aircraft were actually staged on and 25 produced a finding, a recall of 21 per cent, 19 per cent for aircraft-coverage-gap and 25 per cent for gnss-degradation. The shapes are correctly assigned in every case, frozen_position for the degradation runs and not_heard for the coverage gaps, so the two-mechanism design of anom-010 is wired correctly and this is a sensitivity result rather than a wiring one. It is also not a tuning artefact: sweeping the staleness threshold across 60, 100, 150 and 200 s and the contact-freshness discriminator across 10, 30, 60 and 90 s and disabled entirely leaves recall flat at 19 to 26 per cent throughout. The injected disruption is 300 s beginning 120 s into the window, comfortably above every threshold tried, so the loss is not the threshold. This gates anom-005, anom-006 and anom-007. Measured across the twenty rf-sensor-fault runs, whose truth is a broken sensor and which stage nothing on the track side, a background track cluster lies within the fusion radius of the faulty sensor on 70 per cent of them at 60 km and 75 per cent at 85.7 km -- so anom-005 as specified would report possible_interference_zone on most of the runs whose correct answer is possible_sensor_fault, and anom-006 being mutually exclusive with it for the same cluster means the false fusion removes the run from the rule that would have been right. Requiring three or more members in a cluster cuts that exposure from 70 to 25 per cent and cannot be used, because at 21 per cent recall a staged run yields one to three findings in total and only one measured run produced three detections on staged aircraft: the threshold that suppresses the background suppresses the signal, because they are the same size. The conclusion is one number rather than three problems -- the background is not too large, the recall is too small -- and the fusion rules must not be built until it is understood, or three items will pass their unit tests on constructed fixtures and fail together at evaluation time with the cause two layers below where the failure appeared. One interaction found on the way and not to be fixed by weakening anom-010: the aircraft-coverage-gap runs produce fewer findings than their own controls, because suppressing rows can remove the reports that would have bracketed a natural gap, and anom-010's refusal to extrapolate a gap from a track's final report is correct and stays. Refs: FR-304, FR-305, FR-306, FR-308, anom-004, anom-005, anom-006, anom-007, anom-008, anom-010, scn-002, adp-008, eval-002, docs/phase8_detection.md. Discharged 2026-09-16 for the recall half, on three batches rather than the two this item asks for. Batch 1 at the original generator gives 25 per cent overall and 37 for gnss-degradation; batch 2 after scn-006, base seed 20260916, gives 69 and 81; batch 3, base seed 20260917, gives 81 and 95. Parked aircraft in the answer key fall from 209 of 381 to 1 of 62 and then to 0 of 74. The loss account the item asks for is also settled: with the generator repaired, on ground accounts for 11 of the 14 remaining misses in batch 3 and below threshold for 3, with nothing at all lost to the interior filter, to an absent aircraft, or to an unbracketed absence. The on-ground remainder is aircraft that took off or landed during the window rather than aircraft parked throughout, which is the detector being correct. The staging yield across both repaired batches is 58 staging runs of 80, or 72.5 per cent, which is the figure eval-002's campaign sizing rests on.

Local discontinuity rate excess, the track evidence the fusion rules consume. Input: one scenario run's track-gap findings from anom-010, a centre and radius, and a reference time window. Output: the rate of findings inside the disc during the window and the rate inside the same disc outside it, both per unit time, and their ratio as the excess. Constraints: the comparison is within one run and within one place, so it controls for the two things that defeated cluster size -- air traffic is not uniform, so a busy place is always busy, and runs differ from one another; the centre and window come from a detected RF episode (anom-001) and never from ground truth, per api-009; the rate is per unit time rather than a count, because the window and its complement have different durations; the excess is a number the consuming rule thresholds, and this item sets no threshold of its own. Failure cases: a run whose window covers its whole span has no reference period and must say so rather than dividing by zero; a disc containing no findings at all gives an excess of zero rather than an error; and a count used in place of a rate fails the spec, because a 300 s window against a 600 s remainder would report an excess of two where there is none. Written 2026-09-16, after measuring it rather than before. This replaces cluster size as the track side's contribution to anom-005 and anom-006, and the reason is measured: over 20 seed-matched pairs in batch 2, the largest cluster on a staged run beats its own control in 1 to 3 pairs at every radius from 5 to 60 km, which is no signal at all, while this excess separates them. The separation is real and modest, and both halves are reported here because the item should not be built on the flattering half alone. At a 30 km radius the best threshold catches 5 of 20 staged runs and fires on 2 of 20 controls; at 45 km, 10 of 20 and 5 of 20; at 60 km, 16 of 20 and 9 of 20. As a standalone detector that is poor. What makes it worth building is the comparison with what it replaces: anom-005 as specified fires when an RF anomaly has any co-located track cluster, and a background cluster lies within the fusion radius on 70 per cent of the runs whose truth is a sensor fault, so the rule would misattribute most of them. At 30 km this excess fires on 10 per cent of those same controls. The improvement is in false attribution rather than in sensitivity, which is the failure that mattered. Two decisions. First, the form is the straight ratio of rates and not a difference-in-differences against the rest of the box. The naive form is confounded -- the window sits mid-run, where a gap is easiest to bracket because it needs reports either side, so even control runs score a ratio above one -- and dividing by the same ratio computed over the rest of the box cancels that. Measured, it makes no difference: separation is +0.35 by Youden's J for both forms at 60 km and +0.25 for both at 45 km. The correction only rescales, so the simpler form is kept and the confound is recorded rather than engineered around. Second, the radius is a parameter with a stated trade-off rather than a chosen value, because the three measurements above are a curve and not a maximum, and which point on it is right depends on whether a missed incident or a misattributed one costs more -- a question for the evaluation and not for this item. Refs: FR-301, FR-305, FR-306, api-009, anom-001, anom-004, anom-005, anom-006, anom-008, anom-010, anom-011, eval-002. Statistics added 2026-09-16, immediately after the figures above were first quoted and before any of them was built on. The counts in this item are from 20 seed-matched pairs and the intervals are wide enough that only one point is distinguishable from chance. Two-sided Fisher's exact on staged against control: p=0.407 at 30 km, p=0.191 at 45 km, p=0.048 at 60 km. Wilson 95 per cent intervals on the rates: recall 25 per cent [11-47] at 30 km, 50 per cent [30-70] at 45 km, 80 per cent [58-92] at 60 km; false alarms 10 per cent [3-30], 25 per cent [11-47] and 45 per cent [26-66] respectively. The claim that this item cuts false attribution from 70 per cent to 10 per cent is therefore overstated as first written and is corrected here: the 70 per cent is 14 of 20 with an interval of [48-85], the 10 per cent is 2 of 20 with an interval of [3-30], and although those intervals do not overlap, so the direction holds, the separation between the rule and its control at that radius is not itself significant on this sample. What is supported is that the reduction is substantial and that the effect reaches significance only at the wide radius. Two consequences. First, no threshold is to be fixed from these numbers alone: the curve is estimated from one batch and each point carries roughly plus or minus twenty percentage points, so choosing a radius from it would be choosing from noise. Second, this item is not to be reported as a detector in eval-002 without its intervals beside it, per the project's rule that a measurement without its conditions is a memory -- and its Youden's J of 0.15 to 0.35, against a scale where zero is a coin flip and a screening instrument anyone would act on wants better than 0.6, is the honest summary of its standalone strength. For contrast within the same system, anom-001's radio side separates an 8 dB elevation from a baseline spread of about 1.5 dB, which is beyond five sigma. The two halves of the fusion evidence are not remotely comparable in strength, and anom-005's design should reflect that rather than treating them as two equal votes. A second batch at a different base seed is required before any of these figures is quoted as a property of the method, on the same terms anom-011 already sets. Replicated 2026-09-16 on a third batch, base seed 20260917, 60 runs, generated after scn-006 and measured against the pre-registration recorded in thesis_notes before it ran. Batch 3 was scored at the thresholds batch 2 chose rather than at thresholds refitted to itself, because a threshold chosen on the data it is scored against is fitted to that data and would make any batch read as confirmation. Out of sample: 11 of 20 staged and 5 of 20 controls at 30 km, 13 and 5 at 45 km, 15 and 6 at 60 km, for Youden's J of 0.30, 0.40 and 0.45. Five of the six rates fall inside the Wilson intervals batch 2 gives and the ordering across radii is preserved; the sixth, recall at 30 km, comes in at 55 per cent against a predicted interval of 11 to 47 and is recorded as a miss rather than waved through, because it missed in the favourable direction and that is when a pre-registration is most worth honouring. Pooled over 40 matched pairs: 16 of 40 against 7 of 40 at 30 km, 23 against 10 at 45 km, 31 against 15 at 60 km, with two-sided Fisher's exact of 0.047, 0.006 and 0.001. That supersedes the statistics recorded above on one batch: the finding there that only the widest radius separates the rule from its control was a property of the sample size and not of the method, and all three radii separate once the batches are pooled. What does not change is the strength: pooled Youden's J is 0.23 to 0.40, so the rule is now reliably better than chance and still far from anything that could be acted on alone, and the eight-decibel radio signal remains incomparably stronger. The trade-off curve is therefore now supported well enough to choose a radius from, and the choice still belongs to the evaluation rather than to this item, because which point is right depends on whether a missed incident or a misattributed one costs more -- and on the ordering between anom-005, anom-006 and anom-007, which is unsettled. Amended 2026-09-17, after anom-007 was built and measured, and the amendment is in part a correction to how the figures above were obtained. Six decisions. First, the centre and the window come from anom-007's assessment of a zone rather than from an anom-001 episode directly. api-009 is untouched -- neither is ground truth -- but an episode is not an incident, which anom-007 established: the injected elevation dips below anom-001's threshold about one tick in six, so one 300 s incident arrives as a median of six episodes. Measured over batches 2 and 3, the longest episode on a run has a median length of 90 s against a staged 300 s, while anom-007's window, seeded by the episodes and bounded by the readings, has a median of 320 s. The consequence here is direct, because the window and its complement are the two halves of the ratio: a window a third of the true length puts two thirds of the incident's own findings into the reference period it is being compared against, which is the one place they must not be. This also makes anom-013's ordering load-bearing in a second way -- step one's output is step three's candidate -- rather than only a precedence between answers. Second, a window of zero length is refused, on the same argument as the whole-run case already recorded here. A single-reading anom-001 episode has its start equal to its end, and the rate divides by that length: measured, 6 of 86 runs produce such an episode as their longest. The existing failure case covers a window that leaves no remainder; this covers one that leaves no window, and both are a caller handing this rule something no measurement can be taken over. Refusing rather than clamping, because a clamped zero-length window would return a number computed over one reading and nothing would distinguish it from a measurement. Third, the figures recorded above were obtained with the centre and window taken from ground truth. That was a property of the measuring script rather than of this rule, and it is recorded here rather than left implicit because a curve measured on inputs the rule will never receive is not a curve about the rule. Re-measured with the window the rule will actually be given, over the same 40 matched pairs and at the same pre-registered thresholds of 1.79, 1.79 and 1.58: 18 of 40 at 30 km, 21 at 45 and 26 at 60, against 15, 20 and 28 from the ground-truth windows. The curve survives and flattens. No figure above is withdrawn -- they remain the correct account of the signal's size -- but the re-measured row is the one any threshold is chosen from. Fourth, the radius is 60 km. This item previously declined to fix it and can now do so because the question it was waiting on has been answered, exactly as anom-013 said it must be. Two independent reasons, and neither is the height of the curve. The first is that the specificity half of the trade-off is no longer the relevant half: measured over batches 2 and 3, the runs reaching a fusion decision at all are 40 of 40 gnss-degradation, 0 of 40 aircraft-coverage-gap and 1 of 40 rf-sensor-fault, because anom-007 claims the rest. The control arm every earlier figure here was measured against -- the sensor-fault run -- is removed by the ordering before fusion sees it, and the arm that could actually produce a false interference call, a coverage gap with a spurious radio anomaly beside it, does not occur once in 40 runs. With no false-positive pressure at this step the curve is read at its sensitive end, which is what anom-013 predicted from the ordering and is now measured rather than assumed. The second reason is independent of any measurement: 60 km is scn-002's own configured incident radius, so the disc matches the scale of the zone it measures. That is configuration rather than per-run ground truth, and it is the same principled basis anom-004 used for its own default. Fifth, and consequently, ExcessPolicy gains a default radius of 60 km, which reverses a decision recorded on this item and tested for. The original argument was that every measured point is a different trade-off and a default would make that choice quietly on the caller's behalf. That argument is discharged rather than overturned: the choice has now been made in the open, with the reasons above, and a named default carrying them in one place is more discoverable than the number repeated at every call site -- which is the arrangement anom-004 and anom-007 already use for the same kind of value. The test asserting the absence of a default is replaced by one asserting the value and citing the reasons, rather than deleted. Sixth, what this still does not settle, stated because the measurement makes it visible for the first time. At the pre-registered threshold and the chosen radius the excess reaches that threshold on 26 of 40 interference runs, so used as a necessary condition it would lose 14 of them. Whether anom-005 should gate on this quantity at all, or carry it as evidence strength in the bundle while firing on the radio pattern, belongs to anom-005 and not here -- but it cannot be decided without these numbers, and the asymmetry recorded above, an 8 dB radio signal against a Youden's J near 0.3, is what makes it a real question rather than a rhetorical one. Refs adds: anom-007, anom-014, scn-002. Qualified 2026-09-17, by a measurement taken while building anom-005, and this qualifies the figures above rather than withdrawing them. Of the 40 staged zones reaching the fusion step, 26 have an excess at or above the pre-registered threshold -- but only 6 of those 26 hold at least one finding in both the window and its complement. In the other 20 the reference period is empty, so its rate is nothing but this item's smoothing constant and the ratio is a function of the period lengths rather than a comparison of two observed rates. That is why the distribution is so wide, with a median of 3.87 and a 75th percentile of 11.47 on a quantity whose null value is 1. What this does not do is invalidate the separation recorded above. The control arm is subject to the same mechanism at the same traffic densities, since a control is the same corpus window with the same aircraft, so the comparison between arms remains like for like and the pooled Fisher's exact results stand. What it does mean is that the ratio must not be read as a rate comparison in the majority of cases where it fires, and that any consumer wanting to claim an observed excess has to check both counts, which is what anom-005 now does. Recorded here so that a reader of the trade-off curve above does not infer more from it than it supports.

Reportable rule precedence. Input: one scenario run's RF anomalies from anom-001, its track-gap findings from anom-010 and their clusters from anom-004, and the rate excess from anom-012. Output: at most one reportable anomaly per candidate zone per run, chosen by a declared order rather than by whichever rule happens to be evaluated first. Constraints: the three reportable rules partition one decision rather than testing independently, and the order is anom-007 first, then anom-006, then anom-005. anom-007 decides on the RF pattern alone -- one sensor abnormal with its spatial neighbours nominal -- and consults no track evidence at all; anom-006 applies where there is track evidence and no RF anomaly co-located with it; anom-005 applies only to what remains, an RF anomaly spanning more than one sensor with co-located track evidence. A zone claimed by an earlier rule is not offered to a later one, which is what makes anom-006's existing mutual-exclusion constraint enforceable rather than aspirational. Failure cases: two reportable anomalies of different types for the same zone in the same window fails the spec; a sensor-fault run raising possible_interference_zone fails it, which is anom-006's existing failure case restated where it can actually be checked; and an implementation that evaluates the rules in source order rather than in the declared order fails, since that would make the outcome a property of the file. Written 2026-09-16, because the ordering had never been written down and because anom-012's threshold cannot be chosen without it. The measurement that forces it: with fusion reading co-located track evidence and no precedence, a background track cluster lies within the fusion radius on 14 of 20 runs whose truth is a sensor fault, so the rule would claim most of anom-007's runs and, being mutually exclusive with anom-006 for the same cluster, take them from that rule too. Deciding the fault first removes the question rather than answering it with weaker evidence. The asymmetry of evidence is the reason and is measured: anom-001 separates an 8 dB elevation from a baseline spread of about 1.5 dB, beyond five sigma, while the track side's rate excess reaches a Youden's J of 0.40 pooled over 40 matched pairs. Asking the weaker signal to arbitrate what the stronger one already settles is the error. The consequence for anom-012 is recorded here: once anom-007 claims the sensor-fault runs, anom-005's remaining discrimination is between interference and nothing rather than between interference and a fault, so anom-012's radius is read from the sensitive end of its curve -- 31 of 40 at 60 km -- rather than the specific end. That choice is not fixed by this item and must not be until anom-007 exists and its own catch rate on sensor-fault runs has been measured, because the argument above assumes it claims them and that assumption is untested. Refs: FR-305, FR-306, FR-307, anom-001, anom-004, anom-005, anom-006, anom-007, anom-008, anom-012, evb-001, docs/phase8_detection.md, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.3. Amended 2026-09-17, before tests, after anom-007 and anom-012 landed and after measuring what actually reaches each step. Seven decisions. First, the unit this item resolves is a claim and not a rule. It takes zone-bearing claims from whatever rules ran, orders them by a declared constant, and returns at most one per zone with a ledger of what was suppressed and by whom. That is what makes the item completable before anom-006 and anom-005 exist: their only obligation to this one becomes emitting a claim, and nothing here changes when they arrive. The alternative -- a resolver that calls the three rules itself -- cannot be built before them and would have to be tested against stubs, which is the arrangement that let anom-007 pass thirty-six tests and a mutation pass while being wrong. Second, the order comes from a declared constant and a claim whose rule is not in it is refused rather than appended. An unknown rule has no declared position; giving it one implicitly, whether last or by arrival, is exactly the third failure case above -- an outcome that is a property of the file rather than of the declaration. Third, suppression is between rules and never within one. Two claims from the same rule are two events: two broken receivers are two broken receivers, and a run may legitimately hold both. The mutual exclusion this item exists to make enforceable is anom-006's with anom-005, which is cross-rule by construction. Fourth, two claims are the same zone when their centres lie within a configured radius of each other and their windows overlap. The default is the layout's own discrimination radius, which scn-005 validates as the distance over which one cause can reach two receivers and which anom-007 already uses for that reason. Deliberately not anom-012's 60 km, which answers a different question -- how wide a patch to count dropouts over, not whether two candidates are one event. Recorded as provisional: an anom-005 zone may span a centre and its neighbours, up to about 120 km across, and two claims at opposite ends of one incident would then fail this test. Revisit it when anom-005 produces a zone rather than guess now what shape that zone will have. Fifth, an undecided verdict is not a claim. anom-007 is three-valued, and a zone it could not decide passes to the next step untouched -- the only reading consistent with undecided meaning what it says. A rule that cannot tell must not thereby block the rules that might. Sixth, window overlap is inclusive at both endpoints, on anom-007's argument: a window's end is its last contributing reading rather than the first quiet one, so two windows meeting at an instant shared it. Seventh, the gap this item ships with, stated rather than left to be discovered. Only anom-007 produces claims today, so the tests here exercise the resolution mechanism and not the ladder end to end, and no measurement over the corpus is possible until anom-005 lands. What is already measured and belongs here: of the 120 runs in batches 2 and 3, the runs reaching a fusion decision at all are 40 of 40 gnss-degradation, 0 of 40 aircraft-coverage-gap and 1 of 40 rf-sensor-fault, because anom-007 claims the rest. The ordering therefore already does the work this item was written to do, before the mechanism that enforces it exists -- which is an argument for building it rather than against, since that separation is currently a property of what the rules happen to produce rather than of a declaration anything checks. The end-to-end measurement is recorded here when the third step exists. Refs adds: anom-014, scn-005. Corrected 2026-09-17, same day, by the measurement recorded on anom-005: the description of the third step above says anom-005 applies to an RF anomaly spanning more than one sensor with co-located track evidence, and the track evidence is no longer a condition of it. The ordering is unchanged and so is every failure case; what changes is that the third step's trigger is the RF pattern alone, with the track excess carried as confidence. The mutual exclusion this item makes enforceable is therefore between a zone with a co-located RF anomaly and one without, which is a discrimination made on the strong signal rather than on the weak one. Measured end to end 2026-09-18, once anom-005 existed, which this item shipped without. Over all 240 stored runs the ladder decides 60 of 60 rf-sensor-fault runs as possible_sensor_fault, 60 of 60 gnss-degradation as possible_interference_zone, 20 of 20 ambiguous-mixed-evidence as a sensor fault, and is correctly silent on 75 of 80 aircraft-coverage-gap and 19 of 20 normal-baseline runs. No zone in any run received two answers, which is this item's first failure case and it does not occur. Six runs that stage nothing on the RF grid raise a sensor fault, and five gnss-degradation runs plus one rf-sensor-fault run carry a second anomaly of the other type in a different zone -- both are properties of anom-001's false-positive rate and of the per-zone guarantee being per zone rather than per run, not of the ordering. anom-006 remains unbuilt, so the aircraft-coverage-gap arm can only produce a correct non-detection here and must not be reported as a test of the ladder's second step. Amended 2026-09-18, on the anom-006 closure, and the amendment is about this item's evidence rather than its behaviour. The ladder measures 60 of 60 on all five arms with zero zones given two answers, and that result must be read precisely: it is not evidence that the ordering resolves conflicts, because on every arm of this corpus exactly one rule bids. anom-007 returns a fault verdict on the single-receiver types and an environmental one on the multi-receiver type, and anom-005 consumes only the environmental verdict, so SENSOR-FAULT and FUSION-SPATIAL never contest the same zone. The arm built to create a genuine conflict is ambiguous-mixed-evidence, which stages one receiver and a track gap together, and its track half is invisible because anom-006 is unbuilt. So the second bidder this item was ordered against does not exist on this corpus. The ordering itself is proved, by unit tests and by a mutation pass over measurements/mutation/mutate_anom013_precedence.py; what has never happened is the corpus presenting two claims for one zone. Record this separately from the detection results: an untested suppression path that passes because it is never reached is not a passing suppression path. Refs adds: anom-006, eval-002. Further to the amendment above, and recorded so the gap is not read as larger than it is: the arm that would supply the second bid, ambiguous-mixed-evidence, is measurably the right vehicle for it. Its RF stream is identical to the matched rf-sensor-fault run in 60 of 60 pairs and it additionally removes five aircraft, so the moment a track-side rule exists the arm presents two claims over one place with everything else held constant. Nothing about this item needs changing to accommodate that; what is missing is a second producer, not a different design. Measured 2026-09-19 by measurements/corpus/ladder_suppression.py, which closes the amendment above with a number rather than an inference. Across corpus v2, 188 claims are bid and 0 are suppressed. The breakdown matters more than the total: gnss-degradation bids exactly 60 claims over 60 runs, one each, while rf-sensor-fault and ambiguous-mixed-evidence bid 64 each, so four runs of each type produce two claims. Two claims in one run is therefore not rare -- what has never happened is two claims contesting the same zone, which is what suppression requires. The ordering and the merge are both exercised; the suppression path is not. So this item's 60 of 60 with zero conflicting runs should be read as evidence that the ladder correctly declines to merge separate events, and not as evidence that it correctly arbitrates competing ones. The second claim is proved by unit tests and by mutate_anom013_precedence.py, and is owed a corpus demonstration that only a second producing rule can supply.

Minimum episode duration for anom-001. Input: the existing RF-NOISE episodes and a configured minimum duration. Output: the same episodes with those shorter than the minimum reported as a distinct kind of non-finding rather than as anomalies, so that nothing downstream reads a single-reading threshold crossing as an event. Constraints: the minimum is configuration and not a literal; a suppressed episode is reported in the same channel anom-001 already uses for cells it could not judge, because a rule that silently drops what it has seen reopens the failure anom-008 exists to prevent; the change is to anom-001 and therefore to every figure measured through it. Failure cases: an episode exactly at the minimum must be kept, since the boundary belongs to the configured value and not to the comparison; and suppressing an episode without recording it fails the spec. Written 2026-09-17, unbuilt and deliberately so, which is the part of this item worth reading. The problem is real and measured: anom-001 raises at least one episode on 14 of 100 runs that stage nothing at all on the RF grid, and 6 of 86 staged runs produce a single-reading episode whose start equals its end -- a window of no length, which anom-012 divides by. But the harm is already caught twice downstream. anom-007 refuses an episode whose window its own readings do not sustain, which took the promoted false-positive rate from 14 of 100 to 6 of 100; and anom-012 refuses a zero-length window outright. Building this would remove the cause rather than the symptom, and it would also invalidate every measurement taken through anom-001 -- anom-007's 60 of 60, anom-012's trade-off curve on 40 matched pairs, anom-011's recall figures and the batch 3 replication scored against a pre-registration. That is the whole detection evidence base, traded for tidiness at the source of a harm that is already contained. The decision is therefore to specify it, record the reasoning, and leave it unbuilt until something depends on it that the downstream refusals do not cover -- at which point the batches are regenerated and re-measured together rather than one item at a time. Refs: FR-301, FR-303, anom-001, anom-007, anom-008, anom-012, eval-002. Amended 2026-09-18, when the item was taken off the shelf to be built, and the amendment settles one ambiguity and adds one constraint. The ambiguity: the original wording said a suppressed episode is reported 'in the same channel anom-001 already uses for cells it could not judge', which reads as though it should join the unjudged cells. It should not. An unjudged cell is the statement 'I had no baseline, so I did not look', and a suppressed episode is the statement 'I looked, I saw a crossing, and it was too brief to be an event'. Those are the same distinction anom-007's three-valued verdict and anom-005's three-valued corroboration are both built on -- silence separated from evidence of absence -- and folding the second into the first would discard the episode's own window, which is the only thing that makes a suppression checkable. So the findings gain their own field for suppressed episodes, each carrying the cell, the window it spanned, how many readings it held, and the minimum it failed; unjudged cells keep their existing meaning untouched. The added constraint: a negative minimum is refused rather than clamped, because a policy asking for a minimum duration below zero has no meaning and silently treating it as zero would turn a configuration error into a rule that quietly stopped suppressing anything. A minimum of exactly zero is legal and is the pre-anom-014 behaviour, which keeps the old behaviour representable and therefore testable. The value of the minimum itself is deliberately NOT fixed by this amendment: it is measured on the two populations it has to separate -- episodes on a cell the answer key names inside the staged window, against every other episode -- by backend/measurements/corpus/rf_noise_episode_duration.py, and the default is set from that measurement with the figure recorded beside it, in the same arrangement anom-012's radius and anom-007's 2 dB bar use. That measurement is valid across the regeneration this item lands in, because scn-007 changes the tracks and not the RF grid. Built and verified on the regenerated corpus 2026-09-18. The minimum is 10 s, measured on the two populations it separates before the number was written down, and the downstream effect matches the prediction exactly: every one of the 80 false episodes was a single reading, and every one of the 17 spurious sensor faults they were promoting is gone -- across all five arms -- with the catch rate unchanged at 60 of 60 on both staged types. On corpus v2 the false episode population is empty by construction and no episode anywhere has zero length, so anom-012's zero-length refusal now guards a case that cannot arise from anom-001.

Evidence bundle builder. Input: a group of related anomalies from one scenario run, grouped on three axes: simulated time window, spatial proximity, and frequency adjacency. Output: a bundle containing anomaly_type, time_window, affected_area, affected_channels, data_mode, an evidence list where each item has source, finding, and rule_id, and a known_uncertainties list. Constraints: this bundle is the only input the AI layer ever receives; raw observations never reach a model; anomalies on adjacent channels of the same sensor within the same window group into one bundle rather than several; the bundle carries no ground-truth field, per api-009. Failure case: an evidence item lacking a rule_id, or a bundle built with an empty evidence list, fails the spec. A second failure case: a broadband event spanning eight channels producing eight single-channel bundles, which fragments one finding into eight and hands the AI layer an incoherent picture. Refs: FR-401, FR-402, FR-404, FR-108, US-R1, AC-05, ai-003, api-009, scn-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.4. Amended 2026-09-19, before any test, on writing docs/phase8_evidence_bundles.md with the inputs known rather than anticipated. Three corrections, all of which change what the bundle is made of and none of which changes what it is for. First, data_mode cannot be a single value on this object. RF observations are ingested as SYNTHETIC and replayed tracks as REPLAYED, so every scenario run holds both, and a FUSION-SPATIAL bundle draws its evidence from both by definition, since that is what makes it a fusion. One value would have to be wrong and the wrong one is the one telling an analyst which half of the picture is invented. data_mode therefore belongs on the evidence item, with the bundle carrying the set its items span. This reaches further than tidiness because op-001's SYNTHETIC ENVIRONMENT DATA badge is specified to reflect the data rather than a UI constant, and a bundle flattening two modes makes that badge wrong exactly where it matters. Second, the grouping constraint reads as a builder responsibility and mostly is not one. Grouping on simulated time window and spatial proximity already exists, in anom-013, which merges claims into zones on the layout's discrimination radius and inclusive window overlap because one zone per dismissal gave 160 zones for 60 events. A second implementation of near-in-time-and-space in this builder would be a second copy of a rule that already exists, which is the trap this repository recorded once already over distance being nearly measured in two places. The builder consumes anom-013's Resolution.reported and does not re-group. Frequency adjacency remains genuinely this item's, because nothing upstream merges anom-001's per-cell episodes across channels. Third, the unit of a bundle is one reported claim, not one run and not one finding. This item's phrase a group of related anomalies from one scenario run predates the ladder, which did not exist when it was written and is now the mechanism that decides which findings constitute one event; a run staging two broken receivers is two events and anom-013 already refuses to merge them. Two further constraints, both measured rather than assumed.
